title: Commentary on Psalms 7, 8, 15, 16
english: Regarding Psalm 7:8, he says that when the judge has come, many assembled nations surround him, signifying the church; and the Lord says that nations shall be gathered to him, and after this has happened, the judge shall ascend to the height, handing over the kingdom.

Regarding Psalm 8:1, just as the Gospel signifies the gathering of fruits in their season, the Word indicates that the fruits are the works and thoughts of men; and according to Isaiah, he says, 'I come to gather their works and their thoughts.'

Regarding Psalm 8:5, the Maker of these great things, he says, cares for a man whose works are entirely small, and he says, 'I will make a memory of one fallen from you and I will visit one brought to sickness'; for his making is precious to you from the beginning, even though it diminished slightly from the angelic glory according to the earthly body. Glory surrounded him as one ruling upon the earth through the works made by you, and he holds all irrational nature to himself, not only the earth which is easily taken, but also the air and the water, each of which escapes human hands—the one because of its height and the other because of its depth and its passage through the waters; yet he is won by wisdom and mind, and the earthly man chooses the things in heaven and the waters; from these he shines forth according to the spiritual, surpassing the irrational and senseless nature of the animals, being a companion to the rational and angelic through the spiritual, though according to the body [he is otherwise].

Regarding Psalm 15:4, he speaks of the way of the new piety, the bloodless one, and signifies the change in the Holy Spirit, by which we are no longer the former, not even by the same names, but sons of God rather than sons of men. Regarding Psalm 16:6, for having been heard before, he says, 'I pray to be heard by him now.' For Paul says they pray with thanksgiving; for the memory of former things prepares grace for those to come.

The work and the appearance of those who set themselves against him are revealed; one work is indeed a murderous plotting and flattering words toward an ambush, and they are extremely lean in body, surrounded by bones, looking askance with their eyes like a lion rushing toward a prey and sitting in ambush secretly (Ps 16:10-12). Such was Saul toward David, saying indeed that he had found favor in his eyes and was standing by, commanding and having him stand by, while he was weaving a plot and attempting to kill from an ambush.

A secret punishment has been prepared, he says, for them, which will fit inside their bellies, according to what is said against Judah: 'Let the curse enter into his entrails like water and like oil into his bones' (Ps 16:14c).

Again, he sets apart love toward God through [love] toward the temple dedicated to him (Ps 26:4). For he who loves God rejoices in the places dedicated to him, not enjoying the desire through the sight of these things (for it is small to be delighted by the works of hands), but just as someone sees a garment of his desire or a book poorly, being raised up through these toward the memory of that thing, so the lover of God is raised up toward God through the house and the vessel laid out for him. 'This one thing I sought, to dwell in the house of the Lord' (Ps 26:8), which Anna does, and to rejoice at the beauty of the building by looking at it. A house, however, has not yet been built for God. When David saw these things, he lifted the word up to the tabernacle and left it to those able to hear spiritually, to lift the word up to the spiritual house.

In such things the theology of the one God appears, containing the Trinity (Ps 32:6). First, God is theologized as Creator, and the creation is the energy of the Word and of the Spirit; and it is evident that the voices are human where mouth is mentioned, from which word and spirit [follow], but otherwise they are understood concerning God according to...

title: The Trinity and Divine Providence
english: The uncomposed and entirely incorporeal, that is, the Word being with God and the Spirit being, the one being the manifestation of the Father (according to this the Word is named), and the other being the reception of the Word as Spirit from the mouth. He speaks of heavens and powers of heavens, dividing the creation not by the Word for those, but by the Spirit for these (for the things working upon the Trinity are indivisible), but he expresses the same differently, just as in 'Jacob came into Egypt and Israel dwelt in the land of Ham' the entrance is as one to Jacob, but the dwelling is as another to Israel; for from parallel lines he shows the same, and this custom we can find in many things.

In Psalm 33:7 he says of himself, having been impoverished, having struggled in flight, having escaped this danger by the will of God, as he would not have been able to overcome the craft of madness except according to the will of God. In Psalm 33:9 he says, 'I have tasted the experience of things,' which also was present to him then. Therefore, what has happened to him according to the goodness of God—that he was not devoured being persecuted by a foreign king, but was saved from two most difficult and powerful wars—this he adds as a common thing for all, as happening not to him alone but also coming upon others, those who join themselves to God by hope toward God.

In this must the blessedness be, not in any other, which David says in 'Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood?' and 'Know that the Lord marveled at his holy one.' In Psalm 33:20 he commands to look toward the end and to be courageous in the deliverance from tribulations, not to make the beginning difficult for oneself when it happens to be being afflicted. For thus the soul must be prepared, not as if it would not suffer, but as if it would not be defeated by the labors.

To make a likeness to all mankind, he forms a word concerning God just as Isaiah, so that he may demonstrate to God the impossible thing as possible in him, worthy of fighting and arming himself with shield and spear and parrying the attacks of enemies with a middle wall.

And Isaiah shows this in Christ, coming from the punishment of the unrighteous, foreseeing himself clothed in the garment of the slaughter of the foreigners (Who is this coming from Edom, a garment of clothing from Bozrah, and the following things?;). Thus, what is divinely attributed to the Father is clearly both to be a Son and to be fulfilled toward a Son.

Regarding those [unrighteous], it is thought they will become invisible, just as dust driven by the wind, and they will be cast out not by human hand—because the righteous suffer this more from the unrighteous—but this happens through angels, as the Lord says that the holy will go forth and choose from among the righteous the unrighteous and separate them. For now the discordant are mixed, but then they will be divided according to the changing manner, as it was said, and again according to what the Savior said, 'For many mansions are in my Father's house' (John 14:2).

The ways of the unrighteous, he says, are dark; they do not know how they advance (Ps 34:6). This is worthy of being fulfilled, praying that the work of the unrighteous be seized by darkness, just as it suited the darkness, and that they fall by slipping, since they walk a slippery path (for there is nothing supporting them in unrighteousness), and that they become invisible being pursued by angels, just as they themselves do against the righteous. He says, 'He flees to his own strength, which is God' (Ps 34:13), for someone seeks God through fastings and humiliations, turning the whole soul toward invocations of God instead of the indulgence of bodily pleasures, when they occupy the mind according to prayer and enter into the bosom of the soul.

For indeed the things arranged by God are certain and unshakeable, such as that said concerning Noah, that he would no longer bring the flood upon the destruction of animals, which happens according to the word concerning the forbearance of God (Ps 35:6). For indeed the certainty of the word is established through all things, being something great and manifest. So also whatever else has been arranged and established according to the justice and goodness of God, the remaining in eternity has something firm and unshakeable; such as 'I will by no means lie in the Holy One' in David (Ps 35:7). For even the unalterable gifts of God incline toward this. Again, the high mountain compares itself to righteousness (Ps 35:8). This carries a threat of recompense, because it is impossible for anything to happen that is not according to the just, since justice is the guarantor of what comes to pass; so even those now escaping the punitive recompenses, or those not obtaining recompenses at all, will certainly be brought in later; and this is unwavering.

title: Divine Provision and the End of the Wicked
english: It is from God, just as Paul boldly said that God will award him the crown of righteousness on that day, the righteous judge. For abundant things toward life are supplied from God (Ps 35:10a), without which being supplied, life would be destroyed.

It is illuminated (Ps 35:10b), he says, by the light from heaven by the one having set the sun into the light of day; but these indeed are for common use by both the righteous and the unrighteous, upon which also the thing of philanthropy was marveled, not being separated from the ungrateful of the enjoyment of those from God, but the exceptional thing is already and specifically of the ones belonging to God.

He is exhorted to receive God by those being silent, not being troubled by the things present but hoping in the things coming according to the apostolic [teaching]: rejoicing in hope, enduring in affliction (Ps 36:7), and [the thing of] Jeremiah: the Good [one] to a man when he takes up a yoke in his youth. He shall sit alone and be silent, he will give the stumbling one a muzzle, he will be filled with reproaches. He commands to look far off and not to be astonished by the things present (Ps 36:12), and to foresee indeed the destruction of the wicked, but the dominion of the good; and these indeed also at the end, that is to say, in the coming age, since the present does not have the outcomes of these, but rather the things in the earth are prevailed upon by the wicked. Therefore also the whole, he says, the world lies in the wicked.

He says [they] move the wicked themselves according to themselves what is prepared against the righteous (Ps 36:13), as if someone having drawn a sword might be slain by it, and the plot would be in vain just as a bow is being broken by the hand of the archer. And upon David, and bodily this has been fulfilled, to strike David with his own sword which they drew against David. Such a praise from the prophecy (Ps 36:17): to flee indeed from evil, but to practice the deed of the good upon the hope of eternal quiet, and a calculation upon the matter that the Overseer is righteous and does not overstep the ones belonging to Him.

Comparing a body suffering much, he likens it to the many pains and much suffering of the Psalmist, just as it is also in Isaiah, where from the feet even to the head there is no wholeness in him, but only a wound and a bruise of the consuming wrath (Ps 37:4; Isa 1:6). These are therefore the signs of wrath, while sins are the pretext of wrath, so that the sufferings lead to the sensation of sins; and in this way they benefit souls, just as bodies are being moved from insensibility into sensation.

The departure of friends and the rising up of enemies is seen (Ps 37:12), which is also observed in the sufferings of the Savior: through the fear of the disciples being scattered, and through all the bitterness and malice of the wicked used against him, which also fulfilled the silence spoken of there. He says that, having the right to answer the slandering ones, but knowing that the word was not for benefit, he bore the false sayings without returning evil (Ps 37:14). He acted as one not hearing and as one not having the power to rebuke: for what would he have said or answered? For to those not listening, the word is useless, but to God who hears, it is useful.

Men would not say these things on behalf of themselves, but Christ, instead of men, to men—a righteous one suffering from the unrighteous, taking their [injustice] upon himself—would say: 'Wherefore hast thou forsaken me?' (Ps 37:22) and 'Do not forsake me' and 'Do not depart from me' (Ps 37:23), as if this were impossible for him. For he says, 'I am not alone, since my Father is with me.' He asks for the salvation of men as his own, having something in the petition appropriate to the mixture of divinity with the human (this was the passion inherent in the flesh), but also having the dignity of the resurrected nature, by which he fulfilled the requirements of the petition.

And hearing, he says, the bold and insulting words of the enemy, and seeing the authority of the words used by one who ought not even to speak, he was moved on behalf of the dishonored righteousness (Ps 38:4). He says that he has no worthy expectation in himself, but waits for God's and yours, enduring in the present pains in hope of future goods (Ps 38:8). He says that he bears insults now without answering, as if knowing that God intended to strip him with insults, just as David himself brought this upon himself, being insulted by Zemaiah, saying that the Lord had said that David should be cursed (Ps 38:9). title: The Ascent from Hades and the Triad of Faith, Hope, and Love
english: Supplications through which God will be heard to accomplish the ascent from Hades and the firm one toward eternal life, and the support in this [life] through joy, brightness, and hymns to God, such as it was in the [Psalm] 'I cried to you' (Ps 39:2), 'and heal me' (Ps 39:3), 'and you brought up my soul from Hades' (Ps 39:3), 'you saved me from those descending into the pit' (Ps 39:4), and the following: in which clearly the things of Adam are referred to himself. And saying that he brings the resurrection to completion, 'that my glory may sing to you and not be overcome' (Ps 39:4).

For regarding the salvation of all things, the [actions] of Christ are extended, neither having happened through him alone nor standing in him alone. Therefore Paul says, 'If the dead are not raised, Christ has not been raised' (1 Cor 15:13). For if the end for the sake of which the resurrection of Christ was an event were not [certain], then the mystery of death—the dissolution and the ascent of souls from Hades—would be fearful, even while the true hopes toward God exist; concerning this hope Paul speaks, joining to it faith and bringing forth love toward the one so greatly endowed with grace and extending the good things into eternity. 'These three remain,' he says, 'faith, hope, love' (1 Cor 13:13).

In this he says the blessed man makes hope in God and seeks the eternal things, not being enticed by those things appearing to be for a short time, nor deviating into a falsehood from the truly good. For everything that men think to provide for themselves is a falsehood, but only that which is from God is true, which he indeed demonstrated through the whole economy of mankind, having first exposed all human things and then bringing forth the good from himself as complete.

Saying 'myself,' he reveals the Church, and he presents us, the suppliants, asking for mercy, so that we may remain in grace; and the petition for mercy is powerful, for it is said to go not toward men but toward him. For in this way we become those from God, because Christ is in our place, the one receiving the good toward us, just as he says, 'And I will make a covenant for you, just as my Father made for me' (Heb 13:20).

For no power exists for the salvation of Christ's church except that from God (Ps 39:14), since neither weapons, nor money, nor walls of enclosures, nor the holding of the earth, nor anything of this kind is among us, as it is among the Jews; so that a wonder, and nothing less than the other wonders, is that unarmed and unprepared men, being fought against by ten thousand nations, remain both staying and resting. Just as the wonder of the bush was that it was burning and not consumed, and this is an imprint of Christ, conquering through suffering. For the suffering church, not being destroyed, carries all within itself the examples of wisdom and the manifest signs of heavenly help.

To these ends, he says, the church shall proceed (Ps 39:18), having been impoverished before and having come through much poverty from the world, and having become rich by what is from You and having been glorified by the help from You which it asks not to be delayed. And because of the asking, it is not delayed, just as it is said, 'The one coming will come and will not delay' (Heb 10:37). This also is joined to the same hypothesis. For the face of the Savior, and the memory of the passion, and the foretaste of the resurrection, and of the return to heaven (Ps 40:1). Just now, therefore, it was saying, 'I am poor and needy' (Ps 40:1); it would follow as if it were being said by him as an exception into himself.

Even if, and that especially regarding all those in the world who are impoverished through righteousness, understanding is good (Ps 40:2), but understanding in the rich is to consider such needy ones [as such]; but the one truly rich is the one who, knowing and understanding us as poor, is truly blessed; for all blessedness follows the knowledge of God (Ps 40:2). Again, the one suffering on behalf of men says the sins of men's own selves, and he seeks the mercy upon us regarding these things on his own behalf (Ps 40:5), he who releases the contempt of those who are ignorant toward him, manifesting the glory, on himself according to his own power, but on us according to the grace of Christ (Ps 40:5).

This, he says, was through haste (Ps 40:6), previously in the thought of the invisible, and later in the thought of the visible Jews, to cast out the true king, having reckoned that he would come into possession of the inheritance that was not previously [theirs]; therefore they were also saying, 'Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours' (Ps 40:6). They hurry, he says, to kill the righteous man (Ps 40:9), not knowing that his death is a sleep, becoming toward a resurrection, and not a removal of life, but an introduction into a transition to heaven, according to [the saying], 'Life was removed from the earth' (Ps 40:10).

title: The Betrayal and the Divine Form
english: It will be, he says, the resurrection that dissolves the gathering of enemies against us and the betrayal of friends (Ps 40:10). For a disciple has already risen, deserving peace, being counted among those who believe and sharing food, but being a serpent, he was exposed, seeking to seize the wing. The Lord himself also remembered this, saying, as if something had been spoken concerning him, 'But that the scripture might be fulfilled, he who eats my bread has lifted up the wing against me' (Ps 40:11).

We hear of the purity from all evil being removed through Christ (Ps 40:13). The Creator sought this among men; since this has happened, the Maker is found worthy and remains in the good, because all the works of God are very good. He sought but found it in none of those from Adam, only in the one who is according to the flesh from Adam and whose similar transgressions were not demonstrated, but having the divine form remaining even within the fleshly envelope, as the heavenly voice testifies: 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased' (Matt 3:17). The abiding and confirmation before God is eternal, that which is in heaven, and which is foretold in the fifteenth [Psalm] after the resurrection: 'I will be filled with joy in your presence' (Ps 40:14). For he has ascended into heaven to be manifested to the face of God on our behalf, offering in himself that which was separated and alienated from the beginning.

From this, the prudent man understands what the inscription calls for (Ps 41:3): that man has become outside the face of God, so that he might seek the restoration toward the face of God. It is expected that he seeks the strong one, having fallen by weakness, according to: 'Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak' (Ps 41:4); therefore it is necessary to have fallen into the present weakness. For he who loves his own small strength is not sufficient, nor is he able to seek without being left by the true strength.

Regarding those who are forgotten, he says, [Psalm 41:4] they consider entirely futile the return to God, the seeking of God, and they mock those doing this. Instead of the pleasant food, I went before to tears with unpleasantly bitter sorrow, according to that which is said in Lamentations, 'Feed me with ashes.' I am not released from desire because of the separation and the mockery, but I am grieved on behalf of righteousness which is being mocked. Therefore, the harassment and the insults of the wicked are necessary, since the tears resulting from these things are not harmful to the righteous. For upon these is the blessing: 'Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted' [Matthew 5:4]. Thus, immediately, is that of the comfort.

Regarding [Psalm 41:6], 'Let not the present things grieve you, O soul,' he says, 'neither let them trouble you, but let the hope toward God be a consolation, that we shall experience those good things worthy of thanksgiving and we shall have salvation in his appearance,' which according to Paul is the awaiting of the appearance of the Lord and his kingdom [1 Thessalonians 1:10]. These indeed are the things concerning the things to come and the promises according to the law, being higher; and further than this is that which was said by Paul the prophet, that the better thing is to depart and to be with Christ [Philippians 1:23]; but what follows is the discourse of those still grieving.

The separation of the one desired holds the desiring soul in check [Psalm 41:7]. And he says that it is a separation from God, until one sees one's own origin, which is from the beginning; but still one dwells in the land of the Jordan, and the Mount Hermon is as a very small thing compared to that, and one is thundered by such as it were by the assaults of winds and waves, being struck by misfortunes that are brought upon one another.

He teaches the good things of the coming age [Psalm 41:9], the good day in which God will set his mercy according to that which is said in Lamentations, 'Fill us with your morning mercy.' But the present, he says, is toward joy, when night and darkness are the communion with God through hymns and the departure through prayers. title: Psalms and Divine Remembrance
english: In songs. Since it is necessary to offer prayer with thanksgiving, the song is set forth for prayer. For no one, being ungrateful toward those beside him, is strong in his future requests. And the request seeks divine remembrance from God. For he says, 'If I were not in memory, being beside you, I would have gone about in darkness and been crushed by the unrighteous.' It is clear, then, that forgetfulness of divine nature does not touch it, being a change of memory, because the divine is unchangeable. For this reason also he asks, 'Why have you forgotten me?' For no one says 'Why' concerning a passive suffering of forgetfulness, but he presents a voluntary forgetfulness, the thoughtlessness concerning man which is unworthy of the care toward God.

This psalm of the former is inseparable, not even to be divided by an inscription, possessing the same power of returning to God, adding also the guidance through the light that shone, saying, 'I have come as light into the world, so that everyone following me may not remain in darkness' (Ps 42:1), and by this illumination preparing consolation for the one grieving, just as he before him used to make consolation for the grieving by the expectation of what is to come. Since, therefore, the portion of the righteous is fought against according to nation and according to man, and they cannot find [justice] according to worth unless they receive the heavenly judge and protector, just like the justice toward the opponents which he is concerned with, judging all things justly. He also calls upon him just as one who does not judge from hearsay but brings forth the right from knowledge. For this reason he asks for escape from nation and from an unrighteous man.

He says this, having something not different toward strength, and he finds God, such as is also 'I will love you, O Lord, my strength' (Ps 42:2a); then he says also here concerning the resisting ones.

If it is from God to hold fast, it is said appropriately that not being held fast is the most sorrowful thing being from God for one who puts forward only this help, but so that 'Why?' is not as if God were doing something without cause or in vain (for this happens toward our struggle) but as if it were owing to have an end to the struggle through mercy and owing to give consolation to those who mourn, from the one comforting those who mourn (Ps 42:2).

For God has no reason to overlook the righteous, so why does the one seeking what is from God ask 'Why?' as if saying, 'It is fitting for You to take hold of Your own and not permit the adversaries to enjoy pleasure'? Why then is Your own not being fulfilled, but what is from us prevails, just as it is said, 'How long, Lord, will You forget me to the end?' (Ps 42:4c) and, 'What profit is there in my blood, in my descending into corruption?' (Ps 42:5). For if even for a certain time affliction is necessary, but not for everything, and if we ought to be treated well by them in our case, but rather to find the help of God's mercy, so as to yield a peaceful fruit to those trained by it through the God who is full of philanthropy.

Regarding the Lord, it is said entirely, 'Why do You abandon me?' (Ps 42:5) even when it is not worthy of Him to abandon; therefore the appearance of heavenly help is rapid concerning the body suffering for our sake. The brightness is shown by the addition to the lyre and the love in the twice-repeated calling. This remembrance is the consolation. For even if we are grieved by those present, he says, let us give thanks for those to come, and let the sorrow already be dismissed by those expecting God, the salvation of a man who is turning toward Him.

'Behold,' he says, 'we have a king, God, who provides for the salvation of our people (Ps 43:5), and we know that it will be Yours, and in Your will we will be courageous (Ps 43:6).' 'Behold,' he says, 'as a horn we have [it] for the defending against all enemies (Ps 43:6), and Your name, which is upon us, will give a blow to those rising up and to hold us, hoping (Ps 43:7).' 'For I do not prepare myself with bow and dart (Ps 43:7),' he says. For this reason I do not trust in weapons, since even for the fathers these were not sufficient, nor was the achievement completed according to the strength of these, but the work is beyond all human preparation.

He says the former teachings are toward the latter things happening (Ps 43:8). But we are being taught that from You our salvation from the adversaries has always come, and we have seen their power falling into shame. 'Because of this,' he says, 'once for all we cry out to You through all time and in Your name we bring up thanks by which we are saved (Ps 43:9),' just as it is said through Ezekiel, 'Not because of you do I perform the victory of Israel, but because of My name (Ps 43:10.11).' title: The Reversal of Israel's Fortune
english: These things are certain and unshakeable, from which we shall not depart because of what has happened, even though these things happening are contrary to us now. For they say we have been left abandoned from you and, in our absence, the shame that once seized the wars stands against us, and we have become humbled by those whom we previously mastered, and we have been torn apart by those whom we used to tear apart. For in this, even more, the power that once belonged to the Israelites is demonstrated by God, through which, being left behind, they are defeated; just as for man, to be left behind has become the occasion of death, demonstrating that the resurrection comes from God in no other way.

We were seized by cowardice, he says (Ps 43:12), being unable to defend ourselves against those devouring us like sheep; a cowardice which even Moses threatened to bring upon them because of their lawlessness, saying that the sound of a rushing leaf would pursue them. And we have become, he says, captives and have been scattered among the nations, those who previously were driven out from the nations and possessed the holy land.

This analysis of honor is like a man being made of clay and returning to clay; so also regarding the people Isaiah says: We became as we were from the beginning, when you did not begin us and your mercy was not called upon us. They were sold for nothing, as Isaiah also says (Ps 43:13a); and he says they were sold because of their sins, just as Paul says concerning man: I am flesh, sold under the power of sin. But the action is the alienation and becoming slaves to men instead of God, which Jeroboam threatened, along with his people through the prophet Shemaiah, that they would become slaves to the Egyptian king Shishak, and would know the slavery of God and the slavery of the kings of the earth.

For such a thing is a parable, being remembered in the oracles (Ps 43:15); just as Jeremiah says against the false prophets: A curse shall be taken upon you in your captivity, O Judah, in Babylon, saying, 'The Lord will do to you as He did to Zedekiah and to Ahaziah, whom he made kings of Babylon to be burned in the fire, because of the lawlessness they committed in Israel.'

Grant these things now, and most justly: how they, like sheep, were being eaten up when they led Christ as a lamb to slaughter, but were also handed over to the Gentiles as the Lord was betrayed for silver, and by some means cast into death, mocking just as they were making mockery and head-movements when the Lord was crucified (Ps 43:18-21).

This alone remains for Israel as a hope for the calling back of the remnant, which the foretold prophecy says: not to turn toward the customs of the Greeks according to the idolatry they had established, nor to deviate from the commanded way of piety toward one God, even though they were thus humbled and made to dwell in exile and placed under the power of those who kill; which was most certainly guarded regarding Ananias, Azariah, and Mishael, who remained in the fire for the sake of not accepting worship. It is not pious, then, how even the remaining Jews in the present time behave; indeed, it is the very thing that they do not entirely abandon—not walking into idols or even the Greek disease regarding melodies—but the impiety toward Christ is, and thus is most harmfully convicted, that even while not worshiping idols as before, they are enslaved as never before (Ps 44:2).

Having remembered the evils of the Israelites before this and leaving behind the redemption which began for the sake of evils, beginning from the Gentiles and also taking a not small share of them (for many also are those having believed from the Jews), he performs a sort of initiation regarding these things, promising a good word concerning the arrival of the King, who surveys the works of the righteous for his inspection and, as if being heard by them, grants to them the divine fullness, because he has come to pay what is not truly fulfilled in men, which is lawful to divine purity and, from him, a sanctifying reception. He seems to intend to say many things quickly, imitating one revealing these things with the sharp pen of a scribe.

Isaiah foresees his outward appearance, omitting among the sons of men the dishonor of prophesying according to the flesh, while David interprets the divine beauty, which was also revealed by Isaiah through the King that he shall be seen with glory (Ps 44:3ab). title: The Nature of the Anointing
english: It is asserted that his lips pour out [Ps 44:8], just as it is shown in the Gospels that all marvel at the words of grace coming from his mouth.

As then the divine is anointed with oil by nature and not by participation, being joined by its own inherent property (not given by grace as to your partakers), and he calls Christ God, but calls his anointing God, not annulling the human constitution and the relation of the Word to the flesh through which is the anointing of spirit, and the flesh being preceded and foretold by the presence of the Spirit from the beginning and its coming again [Luke 4:18; Acts 10:38].

For if it were said that the Spirit is joined by inherent beauty rather than by participation, then the anointing would be called a result of discipline. And where can anyone show such discipline? And what labor of learning is there with Christ, so that the giving of pains would be sanctification? And through diligent learning, wisdom becomes spirit, but through the struggle toward pleasures, the patient and powerful is sealed by the Spirit.

It is therefore clear that the anointing is spoken of as following nature and not as being given in return for labor, and not as the Spirit being given to man as a wage (though even this is possible; for God gives the Spirit by grace and not by wage), but as that which is inherent to God and man simultaneously, appearing from him and toward him, just as we say when we offer that which is inherent to God and man: 'I will praise you among the nations, O Lord' [Ps 18:4]. By mentioning the partakers, he also showed the manifestation of the anointing; for since the anointing proceeds by participation, because of this it has come by participation.

Since, insofar as regarding the Lord, there was no need for [us] to be naturally holy, being holy and having holiness implanted in the body and by this perfecting the human form toward maturity, but since this was not in us, nor was it possible for men to be holy by nature, but it is necessary by gift and by heavenly grace, for this reason the Spirit is upon Christ, so that He might show through bodily kinship, as being brought from Him unto us for the participation of the Spirit.

The departure of the wicked nations (Ps 44:12a) beautifully demonstrates the bride as the desired one of the King. For this is our beauty, and by this we are beautified, and by this we are made at home with God, and in this way we become exceedingly attentive to God, as one might say regarding the beauty of those who are loved, whatever anyone might say about beauty. The bride is near the King (Ps 44:15), and virgins are near her and are her followers, and through her are made at home with the King, and like maidens following as if upon a bride. In this way, according to the Song of Solomon, the Jewish synagogues were so, being second [assemblies] and following, according to the saying, 'The first shall be last and the last shall be first' (Ps 44:22), and 'The sojourner shall be in thee' (Ps 44:23) for a head, and you shall be in heaven. For indeed those who became the former followers of the law are now beginning the assembly with God for the purpose of being made at home with Him, and this is even more evident from the things being brought forth.

For this is the attendant of Christ, and she enters into the holy temple with Him (Ps 44:16b), and she gives the inheritance and the kingdom of the world promised to Abraham to those of his lineage according to the flesh, by the King who wills and the Queen who approves. Do not the ones who said 'maidens' now say 'sons,' having received the rank of sons, and as sons worthy of inheritance from a mother? The city shall be incorruptible, he says (Ps 45:6), so that God shall be in it, while the watchman of the perimeter ceases from the passing night. For there is a night, until the darkness is removed from everywhere, and not all authority and power is abolished, but still fighting, you will lay hold of them, moving against the righteous.

Nor when, he says, were you given over to the nations (Ps 44:25) having been overcome by God, were you given over in vain, but so that you might know the power of God, having acquired all the nations for His own rebuke, and instead of one land, having acquired every land under His own reverence; for in the same stumbling, according to the Apostle, salvation came to the nations so as to provoke them to jealousy (Rom 11:11). Concerning Israel is the psalm before this, but this is for the nations (Ps 46).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inheritance of the Nations
english: Ascending to Jerusalem and joining with those of the race of Abraham, he proclaims joy to the nations, along with victorious shouts and hymn-like cries, through the appearance of the Lord from on high, which will occur with great fear, because he will hold the earth according to the vision of Daniel, handing over the kingdom to his own saints.

Just as one of the successors of the apostles has said, that the King of the world in Jesus is not receiving some kingdom for his own glory, but for his own, those being made kings through the chosen bride of the queen, as it was foretold in David: 'He shall make them rulers over all the earth' (Ps 46:4,5). He says that he has demonstrated the kingdom to us, all of us nations, and he gave the lot to us, our inheritance from the fathers, the Israelite land, the honor which is with him.

But the Israelite land they call a private inheritance, being given to them according to their race, just as the Lord himself was not outside the succession of the fleshly race. And they say that land was beloved, not because it is able to depart from God to another which is nothing precious, nor good, nor more precious or more beautiful, but because he loved the inhabitants, being the firstfruits of piety in the world, and he preserves love toward them and toward the land to which he inhabited, having nothing that ceases, but all things eternal (Ps 46:9).

He signifies divinity unswervingly in the Son. For this is he who ascends, this is he who reigns, this is he who sits on the heavenly throne, having also sat upon the earth before the ascent, gathering to himself the leaders of the nations and all the most powerful of men, and lifting them into heavenly glory (Ps 47:11c).

“This is your justice,” he says, “not having favoritism.” And Peter says, sensing the calling of the Gentiles, “I grasp the truth that God is not a respecter of persons.” But the wise Israel, having seen the Gentiles and the mercy, will not envy, but will be glad at the judgment of God (Ps 48:4,5), just as Peter and the apostles then were.

“I will touch a hidden wisdom,” he says, “mixing song with the riddle.” How did the mouth not say to open into a parable, but to incline the ear? Or is it that he wants to show himself rather as a listener of one speaking spirit, or as an interpreter, or even through his mouth he speaks the things being said? For indeed, “I will hear what God will speak in me,” as it is said in the Psalms.

But he says that he willingly faces death as much as the world facing this age (Ps 48:10a), being taken away from the earth of his life, but living for God. And the passion of death, he says, did not join with man as being [natural], but happened through dishonor; for he, having been honored by increase toward immortality, did not know, having a good greater than nature from honor, that having fallen from the likeness of God which is in immortality, he becomes like the beast according to death (Ps 48:13). For as the death of this [man], so the death of this [man], says Ecclesiastes, and one spirit for all; and what did man exceed the beast? Nothing, for all is vanity. All things to one place; all things came from dust, and all things return to the dust.

Concerning the coming age, he says, being present, which is the morning of the coming day, the kingdom of the good shall be (Ps 48:15bc), all human power having ceased, but that from God holding sway, when the race of the good is glorious and royal, and the race of the not-good is submissive and a slave, because the strength according to wealth has passed away, but that according to virtue remains, and all the remainder of men in the earth will obey the good, ruling according to God. Therefore let nothing be counted great, wealth and glory (Ps 48:17); for those things not joining with the one who has acquired, just as justice joins...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Grace and the Hope of Resurrection
english: He brings up those who have been brought down. He says that the perfect heavenly generations will sing praises to God's righteousness (Ps 49:6), possessing with perfect words the most righteous and most discerning thing: to rejoice in God not through sacrifices, but through judgment, and to hold this [judgment] for the eternal covenant.

He says that God is not bound by fetters, nor does He drink (Ps 49:13), so that He might attend to meat as if it were food or drink of blood. Then, opposing the true honor of God to the name of sacrifice, he adds [the following].

He says that this [true sacrifice] is the perception of benefits, the confession from the heart, and the fulfillment of vows, which is a debt owed to God by men (Ps 49:14). Doing these things, he says, one is hopeful to succeed with God helping in tribulations (Ps 49:15), so that you may also glorify Him by doing good, being constantly lifted up in thanksgiving.

This is a paralysis of the law (Ps 49:17): to not steal, to not commit adultery, to love your neighbor as yourself, and not to speak deceitfully or harmfully among your people, nor to accuse or plot schemes against your neighbor.

But judgment will demonstrate the knowledge that I will also make you be seen by yourself (Ps 49:21). For each person will see himself as he is, from the hearts being uncovered, just as he was stamped from the heart. Theodotion, interpreting the series of actions, showed through collections that it happens before the eyes of the one who acts.

This was the accusation of the Righteous regarding himself (Ps 50:5). For I do not wait, he says, for the rebuke of another, even if the prophet rebuked. He indeed [rebuked] once, but I see the falling through all things, yet I do not recognize the healing because of mercy.

The request for forgiveness is because sin has become inherent to us according to the first generation (Ps 50:7), being passed down from the mothers who carry us. Because through one man sin entered into the world, and evil is rooted in the first woman, and from her, through those who give birth, it passes on to those being born. It is more appropriate to say this regarding the mother, even though the father also participates in sin; for we are indeed produced spermatically from the father, but entirely from mothers when we are being born, and through the...

Bringing forth into light. Ps 50:8a: 'We indeed,' he says, 'were rooted in iniquities and are born in sins, but to you it is pleasing, the truly good and never deviating.' How then is it possible for men to be glorified by such a judge rather than to have brought forth shame, being condemned?

Ps 50:8b.9: He deserves from pre-existence the grace that is to become [present] and is sparing. For regarding the beginnings, God brings the possible things toward Himself on account of His own purpose and stability, even if the things from us might not at all be worthy, just as on account of the covenant, He pities the race of Abraham which is suffering evil, bringing forward the possible things from the beginning and guarding the certainty of the promise more than the equality of the authority. Since, therefore, [one] who has known wisdom from God and has been honored by this, as to understanding the hidden things about which the Revelation said, 'Open my eyes, and I will perceive the wonders of your law' (Rev 43:18), because of this, he confesses grace regarding the gift of wisdom, and deserves to have the defilement that has happened removed from him, added to it, and this by grace.

Ps 50:10: The Savior said that Abraham was expecting his day to rejoice and to see it arriving and to rejoice, Abraham saying, 'Your father rejoiced so that he might see my day, and he saw and rejoiced' (John 8:56); but David, instead of sight, speaks of hearing, saying that the cause of great joy is being signified to him in Hades by the presence of the Spirit, and that he shall be gladdened in Hades by the Spirit, and his inner parts, the bones of monuments humbled by sin and death, shall be gathered together with the body which is the cause of the resurrection.

Ps 70:7: Sin is weak and a cause of weakness, but righteousness is strong and its defender is God; such also is the expectation of God, and especially the continuous one; and just as, being understood from the first creation, it would not have existed without God, it is rather being trained in opposition to sorrows.

Ps 70:9: Since I have taken up your help in the season of the vigor of age, not the strength of the body, but power; therefore, let this strength remain to me while youth is speaking, and after all human strength has passed, let that which is from you be present, such as...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Christ the True King and the Type of Solomon
english: What happened to David in his old age: for the son rose up new, but there was no elder; rather, already weakened by age and inactive, lying on a bed, he ruled Israel and commanded the nations. [He ruled Israel and established Solomon as successor, having expelled Adonijah, who had been tested by his own intention to rule.]

Regarding the time of the resurrection, these things fit Absalom, concerning whom it is said in Psalm 70:10-11: 'Many say to my soul, There is no salvation for him in his God.' But regarding the fellowship of the righteous, the Lord has permitted such a rising up of enemies, those saying, 'Let Him be rescued if He desires him,' and those thinking that he who suffers according to the will is being abandoned by the Father. Therefore, he says, let the wicked err in their intention, and let the matter appear not according to their expectation, but according to my hope.
'But let me not be far off, but hasten the help and turn their boasting into shame, so that for me the increase of hope and of your hymns may be greater' (Ps 70:12).

The Confessor I do not know how to number. For since he promised to recount the righteousness of God and the salvation that has come through Him, this promise, being greater than a human one, brought these things about.

The hymn begins there, where he promises to perform immediately, shouting loudly the high things of the great God, that men who have been led through many evils might find good things, rising from the dead into eternal life; which is indeed the head of the divine hymns and most demonstrative of God, so that no one among those called gods would mingle with it. For God is the one who makes all things alive, in whom Christ, being the Son of God, is known, saying of Himself that He is the resurrection and the life, and demonstrating this by His work; so that, even if these things are said of Christ by a man to the Father, it is also fitting that they be said of Him by men as to a Son and an image of God; for He is the firstborn, having descended in the manner of a man from the dead, but having ascended by the power of God, being the agent of the return, as He says to the Jews, in whom the exceptional [nature] of divinity is shown.

You surrendered human nature to death, but having been despaired of by men, you gave back a new and blessed life. The glory of Christ is sung after the passion. Solomon is a type: [so too is] the peace of his kingdom, the righteous protection of him, the glory of his wisdom, and the honor [he had] among all men; but exceeding the type, the days of the king remain until the end, and his peace and his fruit become most manifest.

For these things did not at all fit Solomon, who lived for a short time, had enemies, and left no fruit from him but one son, and did not protect the kingdom handed over to him; but Christ's continuous and unshakable dominion and most manifest fruit are for those who believe; and the rest of the things which were typologically fulfilled in Solomon will be more perfectly realized in Him, which the Word will explain one by one as He wills.

"O God, give justice to the king, and righteousness to the son of the king, to judge your people in righteousness and your poor in judgment" (Ps 71:1,2). And Christ is King and Son of David, the Lord according to the flesh, and therefore rising from royal lineage, so that he might establish a paternal kingdom according to the prophecy of Isaiah, and make it divine instead of human; and, as was not in human kingship, he would apply the exactness of justice to the subjects and grant to the wronged that they should not be wronged.

For even this was not preserved in David: though he was most righteous and pleasing to God compared to others, he also became an agent of injustice regarding Uriah. For the construction of idols leaned Solomon's injustice toward impiety. But thus is the King foretold through Isaiah and through Jeremiah: a righteous king sitting on a throne with mercy being established, judging and seeking judgment and hastening righteousness as Isaiah says, understanding and performing judgment and righteousness as Jeremiah says.

The Ally [the Psalmist] gave out: "And they shall fear him as long as the sun" (Ps 72:5), which is in agreement with [the Annunciation] to the Holy Virgin by Gabriel: "And the Lord will give to him the..."
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Error of the Ungodly and Divine Providence
english: A throne for David his father, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob forever (Ps 71:10-11). Regarding Jerusalem, Isaiah says that he will move into the wealth of the sea and of nations, and herds of camels will arrive, and camels of Madian will cover them, and elephants from Sheba will arrive bringing gold and frankincense, crying out and proclaiming the salvation of God.

And through Haggai it is said: 'Yet once more I will shake the heaven and the earth and the sea and the dry land, and I will shake together all the nations; and the chosen of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory,' says the Lord of all powers (Ps 71:16). For the whole inhabited world has also been made fruitful by the fruit of Christ, and an innumerable multitude of Christ's children appearing from every city, like grass from the earth (Ps 71:20).

Therefore, there the thanksgivings of David are fulfilled, which were made for the eternal dwelling of the throne, saying: 'Lord, let the word which you spoke concerning the house of your servant and concerning your servant be believed until an age, and do according to what you spoke, and let your name be exalted until an age,' they saying, 'Lord of all powers, God of Israel,' and the house of David your servant being restored. Thus, the following psalm was written irrationally: 'The hymns of David, son of Jesse, have departed'; for this is the end, and a part of the thanksgiving, upon the fulfillment of the prayers of David.

The second book of the psalms also concluded in a blessing that pronounced 'Amen', just as the first clearly happened. For the end of the former was the M [Messiah] spoken concerning Christ, but the end of this one is the OA [Omega/End] now spoken. And the third concludes, so that we might already speak also concerning it toward the PH [?] psalm, since all the psalms are XVII, of which XA are of Asaph, then of the sons of Korah D, and of David A, and Heman the Israelite is the last.

Instead of 'passed into a disposition of the heart', Aquila translated 'passed by the intentions of the heart'; instead of intending to fulfill nothing of the natural thoughts, they do not even do what they think is good, but they abandon these. For them, virtue is a joke, slander against the inferior is easy, blasphemy against God is ready, and [it is] at hand.

The tongue is according to men. And this is: 'And their tongue has gone out over the earth' (Ps 72:11, 13). [The righteous in the coming arrangement], just as Jeremiah says: 'If you turn back, I will restore you before my face.' There he says: 'And all those who plotted evil, who preferred evil, shall recognize.' For when the good things are revealed in the race of the righteous, they will say: 'There is then the providence of God; and how does He know the things being done?' But the voice of those who have lost the natural reasoning due to the disproportionate good things being against them toward injustices. For not prospering according to reason demonstrates thoughts as if the world were being conducted not according to reason, nor will our difficulties be known. But of the providence which stands over all things, nevertheless, he says, these ungodly ones, who even in prosperity are indifferent to wisdom and to the words concerning God, and in the good successes of the righteous are not yet persuaded... and the patient hand [of the righteous] is a vain patience, being mocked and hearing badly while choosing righteousness. This is the difficult thing of human reasoning: to recognize that the zeal for virtue is not good nor sufficient. And many such recollections come upon many, which the Word is about to heal.

[And to refute the ungodly reasoning, the more godly one confirms it through the person of God; for as God truly guarantees what is said, it is necessary that the pious ones, who are struggling now in the coming arrangement, be more blessed than the ungodly who prosper through the end. Such is in Jeremiah: 'If you turn back, I will restore you before my face.' And the [part] 'And I said, How did God know?' [refers to] those who have lost the natural reasoning due to disproportionate luxury; for since providence exists, they would not be able to prosper in good things if they were becoming hardened.] (Ps 72:24). [The Confessor] later said: 'Honor received [it].' And also: 'I did not cease, realizing silence and believing in you as one who manages well those things concerning us, and thus to you it belongs to understand all things; therefore, take hold of me; you have set a good glory, you have led into a blessed glory.' (Ps 73:4). Necessarily the memory of places [is needed] because of the lawlessness of the people.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Judgment of God and the Victory of the Just
english: For there was no cause for indignation regarding places, and such a one, through the sparing of place, prepares philanthropy to happen toward the people. But this is not as if a certain field were able to be God-loving; for God is not of places but of justice.

112a Ps 73:15b [The Helper thus says: 'You dried up ancient rivers' (Ps 73:15). For the making of springs to bubble up and rivers to flow from them, while on the other hand the streams of ancient rivers are dried up, this is the power of working wonders. This also he says in another psalm: 'He set rivers in the desert and channels of waters for thirst' (Ps 73:17). For it is easy for him, as he wills, to let the flow of the waters participate. But because of this, the word also indicates elsewhere: that for the Jews, because of the lawlessness of the prophetic rivers, the waters will not come to them, but for the nations, formerly a desert, to the crashing of the falls from the rock; and the rock, the divine apostle says, is the Christ, and all the things said contain the type of Him who worked salvation in the midst of our earth through benefits. And these things are thus. But Isidore of Pelusium says in a letter that Etham, a place so called, not far removed from Jerusalem, was watered and easy to reach and shady; to dry this up according to the wrath of God against the Romans is said to be war, just as Joseph in the Archaeology says.]

113A Ps 73:20–22 Remember your covenant and those who were carried away into dark places, lead them again into your illuminated dwelling, receiving the place of the prayer of the humbled by evils and being poured out, and giving [them] to hymn with joy (Ps 73:20-22).

114a Ps 74:2–4 Christ, the cause and creator of incorruption, says these things to the prophet, the one saving as God and bringing the grace of salvation as a man to the Father (Ps 74:2). Therefore he says to you, we shall open confessions and thanksgivings concerning salvation, the sa-

We shall recount wonders, father, when the church of all people having come together is able to hear concerning you, and all people are brought to serve you. And he says of mine, even the discernment over all, saving the worthy of salvation from those being destroyed—those having thought of earthly things being dissolved with the earth, but those having thought of heavenly things remaining like pillars for the foundation of the new creation.

It is not right to dare to be presumptuous or to exalt oneself by seizing upon God or wisdom, saying things terrible and unrighteous against God, as if He does not provide, nor justly rewards each one, but rather leaves things to the risings and settings of stars, and as if the things concerning men are disposed by the stars either well or badly, and already not only by stars but also by the demons worshipped in the heights. For the whole universe has encompassed these things not thus or nearby, but by the just judgment of God, regarding the humbling and the exalting of men, the ones being cast down and the ones being lifted up. [Didymus says likewise].

Upon such an end, he says, in which the evil ones, perishing with wickedness, I shall make the narration of the wonders of God, and I will cast down the strong things of the ungodly, having cut them off like horns; but the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up, having shorn off the uncorrupted power from God. Then they shall be lifted up when they shall have reigned with their own King.
A good end and the victory of the righteous according to God is prophesied to be, after having been brought to a clearer and more brilliant state than the prophecy revealed before this.

He calls the grazed mountains mountains of prey, that is, mountains of food. For food is prey, and in [Psalm] 181 he says, 'Blessing his prey I will bless it,' which indeed Sitias said in that [Psalm] Symmachus. And in [Psalm] 182, 'He gave prey to those who fear him,' Achilles said, and Symmachus.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Signs in Egypt and the Nature of the Heavens
english: Therefore, the mountains of the earth, flowing with milk and honey, are called mountains of beasts and of food, from which he says that God will be seen manifest and exceedingly great. And then the proud shall suffer the things laid before them, not even finding their hands to do anything, as if being carried away by a stupor. For you startled them, your people and those appointed to you, defending territories, as if to join the False horse to salvation, and 'These in chariots and horses, but we in the name of the Lord our God will call upon' (Ps 20:8); they themselves stumbled and fell, but we arose and were upright. The same thing is revealed here through the stumbling and the fall, by means of the being carried away and the hardening.

The Confessor thus interpreted: 'For the fury of man shall confess to you, a remnant of fury being girded around' (Ps 75:11). Since the hot-tempered one, acting in anger and towards wrath in all things, not towards righteousness, is subject to confessions and to recognitions concerning those things of which he sins. For fury is easy toward sin, even daring unto murder, so that the reasoning remaining with him in the soul brings forth strong thoughts of repentance, surrounding the whole soul regarding the things done and said not rightly through fury.

From what is laid before us until the second verse, the word will proceed through the difficult and the painful things concerning the people, and thus leads into brighter things following (Ps 76 argument). He says in the present psalm that there is much time in which the nation may sufficiently encompass and the hope of help from God, unless someone, remembering the former things, might be strengthened into the hope of the coming good things.

Thus, even if he has blessed piously in the first verse, he thus introduces weak reasonings that weigh down men in the longer evils (Ps 76:2,3). For now, for the sake of first confessing to God who received the supplications, he recounts the continuous prayer and the stretching out of the hands through all the nights.

By your power, he says, the whole was set in motion; even the waters groaned in fear, and the abysses had a tumultuous struggle (Ps 76:17-19). And water was being released from above from the clouds, and clouds ran through the ether with much sound, and the arrows from heaven were being carried down; and sounds of thunder were happening according to the airy circle of the clouds passing through, and lightnings were streaming down upon the inhabited world.

And it shook the earth with an earthquake. These things are warning wonders appearing among those in Egypt, those in the wilderness, and those in Judah. For Egypt was struck by hail with fire being carried along, and the Red Sea drew back its waters as if being contracted by some fear. And thunders burst forth in the air and hail was poured down, also against the Canaanites in the war toward the Jews. And it is evident that lightning also flashed together.

Regarding the saying of the thunder sounding in a wheel, one says that it happened when [God] joined the axles of the wagons and led them into the sea with their leaders. Ps 76:19: He lays for us an airy circle upon which the stars are placed, just as oxen circling a threshing floor. For a spherical heaven, according to the logic of the Greeks, is not to be found in the divine oracles, so that we might conceive of the wheel-like revolution above the earth and below the earth. For the divine writings present water below the earth, not heaven, and waters lying beneath as a boundary above the heaven. For He says of the heaven, stretching out like a skin, covering its upper parts with waters. To set the sun from one end to the other, from east to west, and it is said that not even the smallest part of it turns back from the west. And He says of the one who set the heaven (not the one circling it in a circle) and stretching it out like a tent to dwell in (not as circling around); and Isaiah says of the one coming from the ends of the foundation of heaven to those coming from far off the earth, so that the heaven has been founded and stands, but not circling in a circle. But these things are for the sake of a brief reminder, so that we do not fail to be carried toward the fabrications of the Greeks, neglecting the divine writings.

Ps 76:20-21: He says of the divine way that it has no visible trace like the human way; therefore he also called that journey 'in sea and waters,' since Solomon says that a ship traversing the sea is not recognized, so that what is said is parabolic. And there is no longer a journey for God to pass through; for the Hebrews did not walk through the sea so that He might lead them through it as well, but the thing regarding the Red Sea was brief for them, while the thing through the land was much and long-lasting. You guided as sheep your people in the hand of Moses and Aaron. Moreover, even though unseen by...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The fate of the righteous in the destruction of Jerusalem
english: Since the journey was occurring, it became known and manifest to men that I would guide the people in the journey from Egypt as sheep led by Moses and Aaron. Thus indeed the psalm is a parable ...

[Others have interpreted these things thus:] The aforementioned psalm ended in silence, neither seeking nor stating the causes for which the people were so greatly lifted up against their guardian God; but this indicates the cause of the turning away from God from above, which God also later through Isaiah expressed by saying: 'Is not the hand of the Lord too weak to save? Or was the ear too heavy to hear?' (Isa 59:1). But your sins divide you between yourselves and God, and because of your sins He turned His face from you so as not to show mercy, and the following things. Therefore, there is a memory in the psalm of the distrust and contention in the wilderness of Israel, so as to show those turning away from God the evil causes becoming to themselves, as David clearly narrates the things. And it begins royally, immediately commanding his own people to attend to the proper law, or to private instructions, as an Ally interprets; for, he says, such a law is to bring forth a ready exhortation.

And if he says that not the philanthropy and pity of God and much propitiation preserved their succession, but with all passion He struck them, they would have perished, and they became anonymous; [he says] not having accepted their choice, but pitying their weakness as if flesh were rotting and spirit was departing.

[The interpreters have set forth the hypothesis of this psalm differently. For one says that the prophet is stripped simply of captivity and the things that happened to Jerusalem, without specifying which; another says it makes manifest the [captivity] under the Romans which happened after the betrayal of our Savior Jesus Christ; others [say] the one under Antiochus Epiphanus. Therefore, having done this, let us examine some of the sayings.] The intercession against the nations is that, having been impious and unclean, they despoiled a holy land and defiled a holy temple; but against Jerusalem, the contrary, that a city called holy has become a heap of dust and stones.

Which Theodotion says is regarding lithology. And these things can be a remembrance of the election concerning Jerusalem that has occurred. Furthermore, regarding their inhabitants, the [Psalmist] says 'the merciful', that even after death the unburied were given as food to the birds, which proves much and something raw regarding the enemies of the defeated and the slaves of God who suffered these things, which can be brought near to God and for supplication to the Lord.

For even if complaints against the slaves be just, it is unhuman for mercy regarding one's own to be administered by a stranger. And he says also that the bodies of the holy became food for beasts and their blood was poured out without mercy like water before Jerusalem; perhaps indeed because of the election from the beginning, he calls those who fell away holy, just as also the Apostle says of the holy [vine] that those cut off through impiety [are also holy] (because they were of the holy root), perhaps he also indicates the holy ones as being perished together with [the wicked] to the unrighteous, which happens in the capture and the destruction of both a city and a nation, and this has been revealed through Ezekiel; for he says: 'The Lord says, Behold, I am with you, and I will stretch out my hand from its cradle and will destroy from you, the just and the impious, and I will cut off from you the just and the impious' (Ezekiel 7:9).

Which was also foretold more allegorically thus: 'Behold, I kindle fire in you, and every wood shall be consumed in you, the moist and every dry wood' (Ezekiel 20:33); the moist being allegorically the wood of the righteous man, and the dry the impious, just as the Lord himself revealed the true righteous wood saying, 'If these are doing such things in the moist wood, what happens in the dry?'

And if the Lord shared in those things coming upon the world according to the flesh, yet shared in no sin, it is not wonderful that righteous men, being partakers of sin, should become partakers of the misfortunes which come through sins, to suffer equally with the unrighteous being murdered, just as he himself was reckoned among the lawless (Hebrews 2:9), yet was judged by God; such as was the case with Jeremiah, being taken among the impious captives, yet having some distinction also among men after the captivity in the honor from the one who had captured him. And the righteous one would continue to share with the sinners even unto death.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vine and the Feast of Booths
english: Being so, by this the things after death are already useful for distinguishing the separation from the evil ones, just as for King Josiah; for he indeed, being righteous, also died in war while Egypt was prevailing, and much Israelite impiety had already come to pass and did not receive forgiveness. Therefore for those righteous, if they suffer along with the sinners, there are set aside from God things more beautiful after the suffering; and indeed for the brothers and kinsmen who suffer through sin, much assistance is set aside through them, so that because of their turning away, a certain turning of God toward the race might come to pass, which even now the prophet deserves. These things were lifted up as acceptable righteousness before God (Ps 78:4). For if even we are worthy, he says, of those whom we have suffered, but your name is shared in conscience, just as God himself through Isaiah says, 'Through all things my name is blasphemed among the nations' (Isa 56:5). Because like the judgment of beasts, he says, the God-fearing nation was desolated and they laid waste the holy land (Ps 78:7).

Sitting upon the cherubim, having named the authority, he makes manifest the heavenly authority through which everything is subject to him and nothing is able to withstand, if only it should appear; and he calls for the power to be raised because of the remaining silent and quiet and seeing the people suffering; just as it was suffered to come to an end by the Assyrians, not presently, they deserve it because of the abandonment. How, then, to come, either according to the energy or [otherwise]? Because of this he says, 'Come to save us,' just as if he were saying, 'Come according to the saving.' But the 'Turn to us and shine your face,' because of the appearance, the one turned away from God is not able to encounter, unless he first turns back toward him; 'Turn to me,' he says, 'and I will turn to you.' He asks for this from the guidance and cooperation of God, such as is also, 'Incline my heart to your testimonies' (Ps 119:36). For the pious entrust the whole universe to God. But if you appear, he says, 'your face,' and we shall be saved; for the appearance of God is salvation (Ps 79:9). With the eighteenth shadow, indeed, the aforementioned vine covered the mountains because of all the height and surpassed all power that is above the earth, and with the outstretching of the unblemished ones, the cedars of God [were moved] because of the divine power...

To be surrounded, it extends both to the sea and the river. For even the boundaries of the land of Judah are thus called by God: from the wilderness to the Euphrates and from the Red Sea to the Philistine sea. Which [vine] therefore He, He says, brought out of Egypt and transplanted a vine, which He thus made manifest and so widely spread out; why then was it surrounded thus, having been stripped of its protection and being harvested by those passing by?

Trumpets begin at the new moons according to the law. At the new moon of the seventh month He commanded the sounding of trumpets, and on the fifteenth [day] the feast of the booths. And this was a gathering of fruits at the end of the year in the assembly of the works from the field, as has been declared in Exodus (Exod 23:16). And it might be to the one spiritually contemplating the law that the trumpet is a sign of the trumpets coming from heaven, and the fast appointed for atonement in the tenth of that same month is the month of that which is said by the Lord: 'Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted' (Matt 5:4). For the law, preparing for the rest of the booths and the joy in it, made the fast and the humility in it, introducing the trumpets which declare the fear of the presence of the Judge from heaven. Of these, the humility for atonement follows, announcing the coming judgment, and thus the feast for rest comes to be.

And the psalm, being sung at the new moons, let it be even at the time of the feast, differing according to the custom of the law, and for this reason mentioning trumpets at the beginning as a prelude to the feast of booths. Let it signify this: the end about which even the inscription sings to it, declares; when God has gathered all the fruits, and gives eternal booths to His own. For in that end, the good things are restored to the ones being saved, and the salvation from the evils of the present, for which the aforementioned psalms were making supplications to God. [The following things follow after it.]

Removals, that is, of the burdens, of the swellings; for those serving the brick-making, cutting the clay with a spade, they carry it on their backs. Their back, therefore, He says, stood away from swellings, that is, He freed it from the burdens (Ps 80:7).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Justice and the Song of the Son
english: Others have said that the will of God and the mysteries are hidden (Ps 82:4).

Regarding Psalm 83, some take the psalm as having been spoken to those in Babylon who long to behold Jerusalem, the temple in it, and the altar (Ps 83). The rest, according to history, take the temple in Jerusalem in a sensible way (Ps 83:5).

God leads the favor and the obedience to prayers which remains always, concerning which it is said in the prophecy of Isaiah: 'While they are still speaking, I will say, Behold, I am here' (Isa 65:9), so that when we shall enjoy the honor through Christ, the Father thus turns toward us as toward the face of the Son, because Christ shall be in us (Ps 83:10).

Mercy and truth have met (Ps 84:11), when through mercy the nations are called together and through truth Israel shall be restored; for the nations are called through mercy, as the apostle says, but Israel is for the truth of God so that the promises of the fathers might be made firm. Now, indeed, their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, but later the reception is life from the dead, when the perfection of God's favor is revealed to men, when the fulfillment of the promises to the fathers occurs, the race from among them being brought in, not because of their own merit but because of truth itself. For first, those called through truth resisted and did not obey the call, but those called through mercy arrived; then both mercy and truth run together, and then injustice shall fall away completely and the unrighteous shall be driven out from the power over the righteous, so that the righteous may enjoy peace and such as are of one will may be united to one another in both righteousness and peace (Ps 84:11).
To make truth rise up from the earth, justice shall appear from heaven and all good things from God, and all things from the earth shall be good (Ps 84:12-13). Because the [will] of God...

And the Lord brought about justice on behalf of men, not otherwise than the heavenly judgment which is about to judge according to men and to dispose things well, unless Christ was born according to men for the sake of the validation of the facts and received the whole matter of human nature into himself.

Regarding Ps 85:11–13, he says that another spoke the psalm from the person of the Son; for he asks for the exceptional and divine virtue into us from the Father, saying these things from himself which he wills to happen to us, so that the one leading us might be God, according to what is said by Paul: 'Those who are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God' (Rom 8:14), and that we might walk in the truth of God, the true and real worship, worshiping in the Spirit and having only the divine fear, the heart undivided toward any other care, entirely toward the seeking of the true good.

Then he brings to God the hymn concerning the resurrection and the thanksgiving, the Lord himself, since he descended to the lowest parts of the earth, as it is written, and from there he ascended by the will of the Father and by the authority of divinity, and we follow, finding the ascent through the grace from him.

Regarding Ps 87: [arg]: It is foretold to us that Aimán, descendant of Kore, and Kore, son of Kaath, son of the most honorable of the sons of Levi, the leader of the rank of the Levites, sang a most lordly song. For he dances for Christ, just as it is also inscribed, 'A song upon a dance'; and he sings the sufferings of the Savior, the world-saving ones, presenting the person of the Lord in the word, as it becomes clear from the things having been said.

Regarding Ps 87:2: And writing down a heavenly citizenship for the salvation of men, he teaches that, when evils surround us, God alone is to be considered the refuge, just as we also were taught from the Gospels, when the passion was already approaching, making continuous supplications and prayers to him.
Regarding Ps 87:6: Persisting in the things of the likeness...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Unity of Divine Power and the Distinction of Mercy and Judgment
english: He says with words: 'As those who have been snatched away and lie in a tomb, I have become, who suffer this because they were separated from your life-giving power' (Ps 87:5). For it is evident that this was not upon him. For the Christ's body was full of God's power even with death. In this way, indeed, blood and water flowed from him, which nothing of this kind flows from dead bodies.

[Another says he explains the 'Abomination' as an abomination to them:] Just as the disciples were discouraged at his sufferings, no longer hoping in a savior or a redeemer, those indeed who were saying, 'The rulers handed him over to a sentence of death' (Ps 87:5); but we hope that he is the one who is about to redeem Israel. And it is evident that he was also caught in the hands of enemies, being handed over willingly, yet being held against his will. There indeed he also came to evils for our sake; for all those things which are heavy and harmful to the body, he brought. Instead of 'My eyes have grown weak from poverty, my eye has flowed out from affliction, it has given out' (Ps 87:9).

Save therefore the race entrusted to you by your knowledge, and once again turn toward life those men who have each fallen into death (Ps 87:13), so that they may be witnesses of your wonders and of your power; and let them not remain having been blinded in oblivion, but having been remembered again by you, let them be brought back to live.
