These things the protector of men, encountering for the common good of all the race and working out the life of the world by the will of the Father.

He presents him on our behalf, the ambassador and priest, who continues in his standing from morning and through night, and he appeases the wrath of God against us, which he himself received through sufferings (Ps 87:14).

He says, 'Exalt [him] in great wonders and signs' (Ps 87:16), concerning which the Father says to him, 'I have been glorified,' the Son saying, 'Glorify your Son' (John 12:28). He says that this has been cast down into humiliation, when he has come to suffer, suffering for the sake of men and by them, for whom he suffered, being abandoned.

Mount Tabor lies in the land of the Galilaeans, and Hermon lies in the desert toward Sinai. God must be praised, he says, not only by his activities concerning Tabor but also by the appearance concerning Hermon. The strength, he says, [is]...

Let your endurance be revealed, and let it become manifest and glorious among men. All these things are included as if spoken toward one God; we stand in knowledge of His one and only power, which is a perfect arm and hand. Through it, all things have come to pass and are coming to pass, so that it may be counted with God according to the single number of divinity, even while being itself perfect, and in no way falling into [the errors] concerning those spoken of as 'many sons,' of whom none resemble the one whom the Word has truly previously spoken of.

For it is not thus the one and true power, but only a true image and a knowledge of God, with God accomplishing all things through it. Therefore, in its visitation to men, the divine things were joined, and the judgment of God is judged by Christ. Existing as the power of God, yet given to man, just as He Himself said, He distributed mercy and judgment according to the ages. He foretold the judgment from that time, when the King, having come, shall sit upon His throne of glory. For that throne has a foundation like a base, just as it was previously spoken in the Psalms that Akylas has established His throne in judgment.

But before that manifestation, there is much mercy upon the earth, like a precursor to the critical presence, preparing men toward salvation by mercy for the fearful judge who is about to appear; and with mercy is the truth, that nothing untrue or unrighteous can exist within the good patience of God, even if it seems to those ignorant of the future that the wicked are wrongly permitted to prosper, or that the diminished good ones are not clearly seen.

The promise which has come to pass through Nathan the prophet will indeed be explicitly fulfilled, declaring 'prophets' in the plural from one, of whom He calls 'Sons of God' or, as the others interpret, 'Holy Ones of God.' He indeed says that God bestowed power upon David and led him into glory, having chosen him, according to: 'I have taken you from the sheepfolds, from following the sheep, to be a ruler over my people Israel,' finding him acceptable with holy oil for the kingship, and being present to work all things with him, making the rebellions of the enemies void and scattering their armies and putting them to flight, according to: 'I have been with you...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Seasons of Refreshment
english: To all those to whom you have gone and to whom I have destroyed all your enemies from before your face, as it is written through the prophet Nathan (Ps 88:36). And he says that he exalts him by his own mercy and with the diligence pertaining to the righteous. Just as he also unexpectedly obtained victories in wars and was invincible.

God swears by himself, because he has nothing greater by which to swear, just as Paul says. For he says, 'I have sworn by my holy [one],' or as the E edition says, 'According to my sanctification' instead of 'According to my holiness' (Ps 88:39). [These things were likewise set forth by Theodore similar to Apollinaris.]

It seems to seek something greater and beyond man (Ps 88:49), despising the life we live as being nothing, claiming that men move into something futile, not indeed into vanity, but as he deems worthy of not adding corruption, since it is clearly stated that the kingdom will be restored when even corruption is loosed and the living unto the ages is given. For where would escape from death come to us? And where, if not from you? For this would not exist for a man from himself; there is no one who will live and will not die, nor will he be able to save himself from death. But these things seek in opposition to the heavenly king, the redeemer of futility, the same who is stronger than death and a savior of men from death, transforming the futility of the present life into truth and constructing the eternal kingdom upon eternal life.

He did not reject the mercy, but seeks the promise and invokes the justice of God against the impious nations who revile the righteous, having done evil against his own race and having fallen (Ps 88:51); whom he says are enemies of God, yet revile the trace of the righteous king as if it were erased. Having urged these things, he blesses. And the blessing is of one hoping. And of one hoping, he seems to mean the prayers will reach the promise and will not fall away, just as Paul says, 'Is it possible that the word of God has fallen away?' (Rom 3:3).

If he has spoken thus concerning a thousand years (Ps 89:10), it is evident that the span of human life will be the most minute and as if indivisible. The whole, he says, human life is described in a seventy-year period.

Regarding the greater part, he says this: not even this is given in ease, but almost entirely in hardship; for either we are being instructed as infants, or we are laboring as youths, or we are being afflicted as old men. Therefore, he rightly said, 'And the greater part of them is labor and toil' (Ps 89:17). For thus, because the order according to age exists, a little time is stolen away toward joy.

Night, it is fitting, he called the whole time in which a dying man sleeps, but the first is the dawn in which we shall live, when the Lord has appeared and mercy has descended from heaven. It is worthy that the sun and day should shine forth and be given continuously to the righteous as joy instead of the days in which we were harmed, falling into countless evils. These are the Seasons of Refreshment which Peter foretells, to whom he says that our pre-appointed Jesus the Lord will be sent.

Furthermore, he says a thousand shall fall from the auspicious sides, and ten thousand from the right (Ps 90:8), before even approaching and turning away some evil, so that they fall seeing helplessly, and to the perishing he will repay from God, just as it happened to Jehoshaphat according to the promise, so that not having fought, but singing and praising God among one another, he saw the enemies being destroyed. For he says, 'They came upon the lookout of the wilderness and looked and saw the multitude, and behold, all dead having fallen upon the earth, and there was no one being saved.' Near to this also happened to other kings hoping in God, the promise of God being made true, which says, 'I will hate your enemies and I will oppose those who oppose you.' Yet it is not necessary always to think that victories are effortless for the righteous. Since even coming through battle, many times they have conquered, but regarding the most manifest in these things, he says, 'help,' in which most especially God the helper appears to be.

He brought the face of the one hoping near, saying to himself toward God that he placed his hope in him (Ps 90:9). And again he exclaims to such a one, 'Because you have chosen the Most High as a house of safety, no evil shall hold you, nor shall your house be filled with divine plagues' (Ps 90:10). For it is evident that if a righteous man suffers, and the house of a righteous man, [it is] a struggle.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Two Reigns and the Judgment of the Nations
english: This is not a punishment from God against those standing in injustice. It is clear that evils will not prevail against the one undergoing training, but he will rise up as if from sleep, just as it was said in the third Psalm: even if he falls seven times according to the proverb, he will rise (Ps 92:1b; Prov 24:16).

It is possible, therefore, and how much more appropriate to speak of the clothing of glory and the girding of power in relation to the knowledge concerning men, rather than regarding the dishonor of Christ's former presence and human weakness. He himself also brings forward in it the sustaining of the inhabited world for good, which can no longer be moved in any way.

He says that the unjust cannot partake of your kingdom, those who bring toil upon those guarding the laws, by whom the righteous is hunted for capture and he who does no injustice is murdered (Ps 93:20). In these things, the destruction of injustice is shown generally, being established by the justice of God. You said, 'You will not give dominion to the evil, but you will set safety for the righteous, establishing it as a refuge for him and the hopes that hold fast to you'; and what the wicked thought would proceed against the righteous, these things will turn back and upon them themselves; and just as they worked to make the righteous vanish, so they will go into vanishing. This is the end of the vengeance from you.

Let God be known, whom we revere, he who has the heaven and the glory supra-heavenly, to whom beauty is present, to whom power and majesty are in the unutterable (Ps 95:6); that is, according to the incorporeal and divine excellence, since the physical magnitudes of the temples have been granted to the bodily, and beauty to technical precision, and wealth to luxury, and to the nations concerning demons. In Israel, indeed, even if these things were present, they occurred according to a type of the invisible things from the beginning, and it is said through Moses, and it yields to the invisible; especially now during the present Gospel, when spiritual [excellence] is sought and perceived, but also the old [way] is [present] for the wise, just as with Solomon, the greatest and most luxurious, since he was the greatest, having built a temple for the God who spoke, saying that even the heaven cannot contain the glory of God. The Lord has reigned differently then and differently now, hearing (Ps 96:1)...

For indeed, from the former presence he reigned as one decisively condemning sin in the holy flesh and having abolished death. And in the second reign, through each of his partakers, having overcome evil and corruption, so that men shall finally arrive to behold the treasury of eternal life being filled with the life from him, already being able and seeing the glory of his kingdom appearing in them as in a royal house, while making the adversaries invisible as fire melts wax.

Therefore, the earth rejoices again, as it says, and the many islands, that is, the nations, are glad (Ps 96:7-8); then after that, the earth shall labor and the mountains shall melt. How does he speak of the saints, and how does he speak of the adversaries, of whom he also depicts the highness through pride as mountains, and makes the destruction of their pride like the melting of mountains? And to the strangers, he shows fear and constriction by meeting them with clouds and darkness before the sight of the Lord; but to those receptive of light, he says his lightning flashes and glory is being seen, and furthermore, the judicial fire shall consume the ungodly, the righteousness of the Lord being revealed from heaven, as the apostle says. But the psalmist says the being revealed from heaven is announced by naming the appearance of the heavens as an angel, and that he establishes the heaven by righteousness and judgment, as if speaking upon some foundation. He makes it clear that the throne is not a physical thing, but that the kingdom is called a throne.

Those who worship idols through much insensitivity and foolishness, whom they themselves have adorned with statues, he prays will be ashamed, having received sense. For such a thing will be for the beautiful ones. For they will turn away, having been ashamed of this foolish notion, which they held as if they were gods.

An enemy and an adversary to God, the evil one, will not oppose a thing that is of nature (Ps 96:10). For that which is contrary to nature is not divided from the good nature, nor is it possible to find any nature which is called evil; for we do not have such a thing in our knowledge, so that knowing it we might hate it, but we recognize all evil as a work according to wickedness, and the hatred of this, if we think well, we are prepared to treat equally.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegory of the Throne and Footstool
english: Thinking this, they were saved from their evils. Regarding Psalm 98:5bc, it says that the footstool is to worship the universal authority that was then appearing, which holds not only the ruled race but all. The whole inhabited earth is allegorically called a footstool, holding all things in one name, just as Israel is called authority. The throne, being above authority, is allegorically related to the intimacy of God toward the ruled, especially toward the heavenly things, and already toward those on earth.

Similarly, according to Isaiah, the throne is allegorically the heaven, and Jerusalem is also a throne because of the saints in it, in the manner of heaven; this is the evidence that the heaven is not called a throne bodily, nor the earth a footstool bodily, since we call Jerusalem a throne, a small part of the earth, but we call the existing earth a footstool to those exercising authority. Just as the intimacy existing toward the heavenly ones as saints is said to be a throne of God in heaven, being called by the same name as the throne of God in heaven, so also the Lord calls those who received the good seed of the kingdom 'good seed' by the same name, so that he commands those perceiving it in the works to worship not the subordinate earth but the authority over it.

And the Holy One brings forth those who do not run after the false gods of the unholy; and the proper rejection of the unholy from the kingdom is evidenced, so that they may become receptive to holiness. Regarding Psalm 98:9, not only is the authoritative aspect of God to be worshipped, but the sanctifying aspect is already more urgently exhorted, giving the symbol of this through the worship on the ruled mountain.

Regarding Psalm 100:8, the first part indicates the diligent, just as God sends the prophets with diligence, as he says 'Rising, he sends'. And the removal of the evil ones is lawful: 'Remove the evil from among you' (Psalm 100:8). And this has not ceased concerning us, even if it happens in a punitive manner.

For the wicked are separated, and unless it be by death, [they remain so] until repentance. This is similar in power to what is said of Solomon's prayer, praying regarding the coming tribulation of the people, so that they might be heard while entreating in it (Ps 101:3); except that the speaker, speaking in his own person, says all things and that Israel might not be seen by God, which it risked suffering because of its own wickedness, and also the long-term affliction.

God's servants' entreaty and God's pity make the time; no other cause exists such as those destined through the ages in Greece. This is what he himself says through Isaiah: 'In an acceptable time I heard you' (Isa 65:24); and Paul also writes about the fulfillment of the time when the Savior arrived, asserting: 'Behold, now is the acceptable time' (2 Cor 6:2). For chiefly the descent of the Savior happened through the culmination of the ages.

Since the Savior has come to take away the sin of the world, it was not fitting for the one who is far-off to come and suffer for a few sinners. When the time was divided according to which it is said, 'All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God' (Rom 3:23), and there was no longer a righteous man on earth understanding and seeking God, the one who enjoys the grace of God above all of them, tasting death on behalf of all, came.

These things could also be said: it was necessary for the God who provides for their salvation to prevent the turning of the human race toward wickedness. And indeed this happened through many mechanisms. Through the sending of patriarchs who were able to benefit the life of men by their own polity, but as they were turning toward wickedness and despising the law given by Moses, and despite the sending of prophets and the appearance of angels to them, God did not cease providing for their salvation. And yet, nothing happened more than they were being ground down for the increase of wickedness. Since therefore every medicine and help was being brought in through the only-begotten [...]
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Works of Christ and the Spirit in Creation
english: He strove against their incurable diseases; after all those things the Savior came appropriately, healing every disease and every weakness, even to raise up their corruption and death. For this reason the Savior shone forth the truth in the times of Augustus, when the time was fulfilled so that the things of human salvation happened accordingly.

Concerning this the present word says: 'It is a time to have mercy on Zion, O Lord, and You, rising on Your own, will have mercy on her' (Ps 102). Thanksgiving was necessary to follow the preceding prophecy. This too is arranged through this song: the mercy of God and the critical justice are glorified, that through mercy He will rescue the people from the wrongdoers; the removal of corruption, and the grace preserved for successors, and the kingdom of heaven that will pass over all things.

It is not that the heaven surrounds the whole thing and covers it, but it roofs the earth spread out around it, being covered from above by waters in a permanent and firm standing (Ps 103). It is evident, then, that the 'Extending' and 'Roofing' and 'Making' is instead the 'one who extended' and 'one who roofed' and 'one who made.' So it is also with the 'Forming' spirit of man within him; the forming having occurred by God once for the earth, and the results from it happen forever, just as it is said, 'My Father is working until now, and I am working' (John 5:17). And 'I am the Being' would also contribute to this, as the works are not non-existent but are becoming, having the nature of the becoming, and therefore their being is understood in the becoming and is not actually existing like the maker. This is permeated through the Holy Trinity being creative.

Regarding the wonderful thing, it says of the founding of God's power: the earth, being the heaviest element, having been set beneath the waters and remaining immovable for an age, is not perhaps supported by the abyss that lies beneath, nor is it settling, but is covering [the abyss] in the manner of garments, so that the seat may be unutterable and of God's power, not of the nature of elements (Ps 103). The earth gives these things, springs of water gushing from the beginning by the power of God (Ps 103), and says that many things are driven into disappearance by the fear of God, which is stated more clearly in the seventy-third [Psalm]: 'You burst the springs and...'

Rivers, you dried up other rivers. He marvels also at the position of the mountains, having been raised unchangeably over the plains and not being dragged down by the descending mist to cover the underlying things, according to the Erusi: 'Cover us, O mountains' (Ps 103:13).

He calls the air of the high heavens the work of God, just as it is over one house of the whole world. And he calls the rain the work of the Son, from which the earth bears fruit in abundance (Ps 103:17). And he calls the lifting up of the waters from the sea the work [of the Son] (Ps 103:17b).

And concerning the wild donkey it is said through Jeremiah: 'Even the wild donkey in the heavens has known its times' (Ps 103:26b). And regarding his calming, it is said that God [calms him], that is, to set his cunning to nothing. For God laughs at everything that opposes him, because it is placed in vanity and childishness because it is easily burned, just as it is said concerning the Egyptians: 'How many follies I have performed against the Egyptians' (Ps 103:27-28).

[Others will take the provided text regarding the food provided to the animals. For when this is present, it is abundant and rejoices; but when it is absent, it is pressed and poured out by the lack of necessities (Ps 103:29-30).]

This is the work of Christ, who also says that resurrection is to be, and life, and he promised to raise up all; and when he was present, he gave life to whom he wished, so that what is said is: of the Father in the beginning, of the Son in the working-out, and of the Spirit in the participation, being a partaker of him and as if being brought through the Son into the life of all, according to: 'He will give life to your mortal bodies through the Spirit who dwells in you' (Ps 103:31). The Spirit is indeed life-giving, through which he works life, and God-making, through which he gives participation and the human spirit is of the same name according to its formation by him (Ps 103:32).

Eternal is the glory of him who preserves his works forever; and since the glory is eternal, the things being glorified are eternal (Ps 103:33). The magnitude of the glory is shown by the awe of the creation, and the subjection is signaled by the awe. Thus the psalm says that the sea is made subject by being terrified (Ps 103:34). For what fears, submits; and the subjection of the earth is the trembling of the oversight of God, and the smoking of the mountains, as if they were burning, which was seen bodily on Sinai (Ps 103:33-34). This is the gain of life; for this it is worthy to live; therefore death is terrible, the one silencing the...
The text ends abruptly mid-clause.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Kindness and Severity
english: Death is a loss, because there is no one in death remembering you, and life is merely existence because those living, he says, will praise you. For we have being through connection to the One who is, and separation is corruption. My discourse pleased him, and I shall be glad in the Lord; and he is worthy of prayer, so that God may be glad through our hymns, and we may have joy through them in every way. Even if all this were such that all our actions were a hymn to God, God would be glad for us, just as he was glad from the beginning.

One should not ignore, he says, that he is the Lord our God, whose providence governs the whole universe with divine judgments, so that nothing happens unsuitably or without his providence (Ps 104:7). [The plagues] were applied without distinction to the ranks of the plagues and he does not leave all [of them] out, for I think the power of God and the ever-spoken wonders are shown; and it is necessary that God's power be made known, and not an uninterrupted history of events (Ps 104:15).

He says the frogs did not come simply to the land, but into the houses, and the most prominent of the houses and their innermost parts, so that their onslaught would be unhindered and most violent, with no one, not even the strongest, being able to prevent it (Ps 104:27). It is also paradoxical that the dust and the lice were poured out over the whole earth and stood at the borders, not spreading further, as if the judgment were being carried out only in Egypt. Therefore, the bloodletting of the river also happened to stop at the borders, while in the neighboring regions the flows were such that, according to the Egyptians, the punishment was the removal of the river's prosperity (Ps 104:37).

Regarding the salvation given and the prosperity, he says [of] the power from God which led the Egyptians away, they ask to provide many and costly things for those about to leave the land. And it is great also to be delivered from suffering, while the land suffers most, until one [is safe] (Ps 105:14). When they tested God in a waterless place, being unchangeable and not forgetful, he did not fail them; he gave them...

Not only regarding their petition, but also when they were ascending in the Red Sea, and then He made His power known to them; but when they mocked Moses and Aaron in the camp, the earth suddenly opened and swallowed them up. For it was necessary that the servants should not be despised.

But also, since kindness and severity are both with Him, according to 'Behold then the kindness and severity of God' (Rom 11:22), first the things of kindness were provided to them; but as they were not able through it, following that, He met them with the medicine of the cauterizer.

Regarding Moses, indeed, those concerning Dathan and Abiram mocked, saying, 'Has God spoken to Moses alone? Has He not also to us?' and Korah and his assembly, daring to bring strange fire and sacrifices to God in the land of the sanctuaries. But for those who spoke against Moses, the earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered the assembly of Abiram; and for Korah and those with him who were about to offer their incense, a flame proceeding from the Tabernacle burned them.

According to justice, the term is of destruction, but according to philanthropy, the remission is of saving. Regarding the remission, the embassy gave space because of the holiness of the one embassying and the providence for the sake of the world, through which the ambassador pleaded, so that the grace of God regarding Israel might not be considered insufficient; and because of the memory of the fathers and the promise to them, which Moses reminded [God] while pleading, for according to their impiety and the foreknowledge of all their evil, they would have been destroyed.

And the dispute concerning the earth is more ancient than the stand of Korah and Dathan, but greater and more impious, contending against the promise of God and not striving for the healing of God; so it is fitting that it is arranged through the cowardice occurring from the aforementioned impiety toward God, just as that [dispute] occurred through small-mindedness, a despairing of the success of the cowardice, just as the small-mindedness because of the separation of Moses was making a despairing of the return of Moses. For not only desires, but also cowardices and small-mindednesses of those owing to God and those owing to men are taken away, the endurance...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Allegory of the Exodus and the Sea
english: Obstacles to honor are produced by disobedience to God and by disorder among men, as the fleshly nature mourns the spiritual [nature] and the beauty beside it vanishes through its own pleasure. But the God of discipline leads things through certain ways; the end of discipline is the correction of man toward the right through the leadership of the spirit, and the obedience of the flesh.

For this reason, he placed the provision of pleasures as a teacher, so that the desire of these might be made subject to the intellect according to the will of God, and he led [them] through dangers, training [them] to endure what is otherwise to be fled from through the hope toward God which is fitting for those who think rightly. And since men are more fleshly in the present state, first he relents from justice toward the disobedient and small-souled, but later, toward a return, he punishes.

Since, indeed, not punishing those shrinking from and arguing against the Red Sea, he punishes those who did not dare to follow him toward the promised land. For it was a manifest sign of unbelief. For to have seen so many and such wonders, to dare [to rebel] against all things was not just by the power of salvation.

And indeed, since having punished the Egyptians less, even though they were more impious, in some parts, he punished more severely with the death of the people in the disobedience of all the people of that time regarding the distribution of the land, because through the former justice they were not made wise and they remained to test God even more. Regarding Psalm 105:28, he did not say the cause of idolatry was that which was fornication, leading them into participation in reverence (for this was related to gluttony), but the result condemns it, for the sake of which also the law spoke of the mixing with women of foreign nations, lest they should fall into participation in impiety through the sympathy of the women, which indeed happened. For it led them so far into madness, as to be initiated into the things of Beelzebub and to be joined in sacrifices performed by the dead.

In Psalm 105:46-47, in this he shows that the return of the captives through mercy would not remain unshaken, having brought a prayer concerning the gathering from the nations and ending in this, so that they might find the salvation from God himself to be firm and immovable and through all things give thanks to the Savior and the [life] in God.

They have joy. And it is necessary for mercy to receive those after their present unbelief, as the apostle says, so that having been petitioned, they may dance to God all the days, as Zechariah foretells (Ps 106:6).

He says these things concerning the Jews: first, having been freed from the oppression in Egypt by crying out to the Lord, now, being subject to the same things and being delivered from all kinds of wandering, if they would cry out to the Lord, they might happen to reach the perfect liberty through Christ. And this is the same allegory, whence it does not seem at all that these things are being allegorized. For the words spoken do not suit the idea of the same people wandering in a desert and being bound in a dark prison. But it is clear according to Isaiah, he who says to those in bonds, 'Come forth,' and to those in darkness, 'Be uncovered,' concerning which Zechariah [says] that by His blood His covenant sent the prisoners out of a pit without water. Christ is therefore Savior from the Father, and Father through Christ. But Israel is being covered by death now, and is bound by humility and by the necessity of slavery. For the covering is a shadow, but humility is poverty, and necessity is iron. And for the Gentiles, they establish them being cast into a land of the nations, the poor from the beginning, concerning whom the 105th Psalm says, 'The poor shall eat and be satisfied' (Ps 105:9).

Allegorizing the evils of the Jews as wandering, famine, thirst, darkness, and bonds, he uses now an allegory of mariners: the disturbances in the sea and the transformations from these into prosperity, and leading them even unto a prosperous salvation through these labors; and he who has received the labors shall find rest, not without God having been disturbed into waves their former calm, but they show it by a divine command, just as one having raised a storm by command and having shaken their former prosperous sailing with the waves, by which they are being lifted up to a height and tossed down, as it happens to be in the sea, being humbled and being poured out and being tossed about by an ecstasy; then to experience a change by the wind, whenever God might command this, and He releases the violence of the winds into a gentle breeze and quiets the sound of the waves, where...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Eternal King and Priest
english: They shall have the joy from the wilderness, and that which they long for they shall reach: a landfall into a harbor, upon which it is fitting to confess thanks to God in the church of the people and in the seat of elders, to hymn Him on account of, indeed, sins, as it was foretold, having delivered the nation to the waves, but having transferred them by mercy into good things. And mercy itself makes manifest that one has been brought forth from sins. For the unworthy of good things are pitied, but regarding the evil ones, they are pitied; of which indeed the matter is not common, not as it often happens in the sea, where the good ones are tossed and shipwrecked, just as also Paul (Acts 27), and the bad ones are brought out of storms, being common to both sides in the things happening, so that being examined in the same things, the difference in judgment might be made manifest toward which later a right and just retribution toward their own works has been pre-witnessed. Not indeed is the word about the many seas, but about the one being tossed by sin and by mercy reaching into the harbor of the people, of which also the church is for confession and the seat of elders for a hymn to God.

Mercy toward men which He asks on behalf of men (Ps 108:21). He who, not being by Himself in need of mercy, being good in helping the worthy with terrible things, and not measuring out the equal, but for all things has come to Christ and is pitied on our behalf; for as He is, He also as a poor and humble man is pitied, and as being in disturbances, as He partook of the one being tossed in evils of nature, and as retreating into obscurity as far as His bodily appearance failed, and as having been moved and having been helped, as if one of the most deaf, according to those having snatched Him away, He gave Himself up; and the weakness from fasting and the sharpness from lack of food He brings from us into Himself, placing nothing between us and Himself, and He speaks a reproach upon these things, the reproach from those fighting which He now has from us, those mocking in His name.

That the whole world will be permeated shows the powerful authority of the divine King, having begun from Jerusalem according to 'I have been made king upon his holy Mount Zion' (Ps 109:2), and all will obey and serve.

Apollinaris, placing the interpretation of Symmachus, says: the continuousness of the peak and the unfading, being compared to eternal life by morning dews, just as the released life was compared to a shadow to a reclining one, 'The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind' (Ps 109:3), and the following.

An eternal priest, the one living eternally, a stable priesthood having been made firm by an oath (Ps 109:4), is a type of Melchizedek, whose death is not made manifest, as a sign of the non-existence of death; and now, having been revealed as king, he is now also shown as priest, which is impossible in Israel and by law. It was typified in Melchizedek and this too.

For it is evident how Christ, even before being exalted by men, was exalted, being in the form of God and having descended from heaven (Phil 2). But the symbol of lowliness is the journey and drinking water from a stream; and we indeed see the Lord walking and asking for drinking water from the Samaritan woman (John 4).

Regarding Psalm 110: It is said in the present that the hymn is through short [verses], and through the twenty-two elements of the Hebrews, the first sounds of the verses precede according to the Hebrew from first to last, that is, from Aleph to Tav, having a grammatical propriety of such a composition, which is called a preparation for the learning of letters and books, just as the psalms immediately and clearly exhort to the study of the law, since Moses himself commanded from above the same and having ordered to be made introducers to letters and to command the children to teach the law, because they had the learning through hearing, not through the Spirit the wisdom as those being perfected according to Christ.
He says, the righteousness of the blessed is not being extinguished (Ps 111:9), nor...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Pattern of Christ and the Path of Virtue
english: To stand even in the present and to be extended into the coming age, in which age His horn shall be lifted up in glory; that is, the kingdom which he shall be honored to attain from the saving promises. For it is customary in Scripture to call the kingdom 'Horn' (Ps 113:16).

But it is also just to establish those who worship most beautifully and consider the incorporeal as divine into something like themselves. And this would not appear to them as a curse justly, but rather becoming God is worthy of a prayer, just as they think they possess that which they marvel at.
For man is empty and a vapor in his being and non-being, because he seems to be, yet is not, but rather turns toward an image of life rather than in truth (Ps 115:2).

It is necessary for a release from the bonds of Hades, so that the God of the living and not a God of the dead may be ours, and we may be His ministers in the heavenly church, into which we return, fleeing the bonds of death (Ps 115:7-10).

He indeed rejoices as one having heard, and hopes as one receiving help; and he is strengthened by hope toward not fearing the plots of men nor marveling at their powers, but foreseeing their fall. These things indeed were formerly concerning Israel, with the other nations lying upon it (and the word is spoken hyperbolically), but after these things concerning the church from the nations, being fought against by the rebellions of the unbelievers. For those having believed in each nation were enduring the disturbances and dangers from the unbelievers, but nonetheless, even these, having been emboldened by God, conquered their opponents (Ps 117:7-9).

Those fighting serve God, yet they exult in human power and in human leadership; but those taking hold of the fear of God are emboldened by the help of God, and having lost this, they find a strength even stronger; and most magnificent are those who defend themselves in the name of Christ and of the Lord alone against enemies both visible and invisible (Ps 117:10-11).

He sings of the Lord's clear manifestation, through which salvation is restored to all, having said 'God' according to the Father and 'Lord' according to the Son's name, because both the Lord is God and the God is Lord; having appeared as Lord, He ruled over us and them into life, according to the [text breaks] that He might rule over the dead and the living, and the opposites into judgment (Ps 117:27a).
According to the abolishing of all authority and power (Ps 117:27bc).

The establishment of a feast is protected by a multitude of priests placing [sacrifices] upon the altar even unto its horns and the other projections. And as proceeding upon our own priests, the Word clearly shows those presenting themselves as a living sacrifice, truly pleasing to God according to a type of Christ (Ps 118:1), whose multitude also fills the altar even to the uppermost height which joins with the heavenly angels, through the same power which lifts the heavenly things toward the height and lifts up the earthly things by the manner of an altar receiving those approaching God.

These indeed were those not having walked in the counsel of the ungodly nor standing in the way of sinners (Ps 118:1bc), but grasping the law and the course in this. And he says 'blameless,' not meaning altogether falling away from faults and sins. For this was appointed for Christ and for the partakers of Christ through him; but for those, the blamelessness was judged by the forgiveness from God and not by the exactness regarding the outward regulations. For God does not require the impossible, but legislates by exposing what is lacking, and he forgives the weak, knowing them, and providing salvation through the then-yet-to-come participation in Christ, the powerful God. It is therefore fitting for us to live blamelessly according to Christ.

Since there were many oppositions toward virtue (Ps 118:5), just as there are stumbles on a road, he asks for the removal of these. For thus the road is made smooth by the removal of those who obstruct, according to 'Cast out of the way of my people the worms'; just as for the divine David a woman became a stumbling block and an unseasonable fall in a spectacle, for another a morsel for pleasure being seen, such as for Esau, for another glory just as for Saul, for another property just as for Ahab; all of which are necessary for God who is preparing the way, which should pack these things and maintain the beautiful inclination, even though the more violent things of the intention were pulling and, as if unwearying, were flowing because of their nature.

But for us, regarding the divine Spirit, it will be a matter of not being ashamed (Ps 118:6), when we see ourselves joined to him everywhere and in no way turning toward the flesh, nor being dragged down from a height of falling. In having learned the judgments of the...
In having learned the judgments of the...
