title: The Utility of Divine Wisdom and the Vanity of Mind
english: I will keep your statutes of righteousness. He says it asks for understanding, and it is promised that this will not be unfruitful. For I will not only learn, he says, but I will also keep your statutes (Ps 118:10).

Akyllas says, 'Let me not be ignorant' [toward what we are saying]. One using desire regarding the law fears the lack of understanding, which turns the zeal of many into the opposite. And in those things in which they seem to be upright, they have stumbled according to that which is said by Solomon: 'There is a way that seems right to men, but its end comes into the pit of Sheol' (Prov 14:12). For understanding does not come immediately from memory, but from the divine illumination; and the statutes are those capable of justifying (Ps 118:12b).

Pride is the mother of lawlessness. For through this they do not endure to obey the commands of God, such as the disobedient people who say, 'We will not be ruled, nor will we come to you anymore.' This shows his own readiness toward obeying the commandments to God. For he understands the guilty, and he will rebuke those who are disobedient and unruly through pride.

He prays to flee from the ignominy which is before God, which the Lord shows to be most fearful, saying that those who have shamed Him will be shamed (Ps 118:22). The lawful man, pointing out the opposite of this, says here mocking, [that they] are not to depart from the study of the holy oracles and the correction through them, and shortly after, he says, 'I have spoken in your testimonies against kings, and I was not ashamed' (Ps 118:23); such is also Paul, saying, 'For I am not ashamed of the gospel' (Rom 1:16).

What he himself says is to be a sacrifice to God, a broken and humbled heart, he says has now been fulfilled, having brought the soul down as to the ground and having been humbled voluntarily, just as regarding involuntary humbling it is said, 'Our soul was humbled into dust, our womb clung to the earth' (Ps 29:9). Having brought himself as becomes a humble man, he seeks from God a reward: a life-conduct according to the law and life according to the word of God (Ps 118:25). And this very thing is humbling: not to set the good life upon oneself, but to seek it from God.
To do all things greatly as in the eyes of God and to say these things and to recount (Ps 118:26-27).

And to ask for a corrective or confirming revelation regarding these things, while there remains for him also the benefit to others by conversing with a more divine understanding and announcing the wonderful benefit which God has stored up for those doing what is holy. For he who teaches concerning righteousness also teaches concerning the end, which is laid up for it, being something wonderful and unexpected, that God greatly and beyond measure rewards. Paul also conversed concerning self-control and righteousness and the judgment that is to come, as the ruler becomes a terror. Instead of 'I will not wander,' one [says] 'Akylas will preach,' and the other 'Symmachus will explain.'

If the heart of man is carefully directed toward evil from youth, it is necessary that God, by moving it toward righteous commands—that is, by leading our choice toward economies and realities and the illumination of the Holy Spirit—[intervene].

Vanity is the madness concerning visions, the contemplation concerning non-existent things, and the absurd fantasy according to the intellect, which Paul makes clear, saying, 'Being darkened in the vanity of their mind, having been alienated from the life of God' (Rom 1:21). See that 'vanity of mind' is called so when one has a mind and does not use it for the contemplation of the truths, but provides it to the binding Satan. This, therefore, he says, 'Turn my eyes away, lest I see vanity'; for this is by the grace of God. For in this way one will be able, having turned away from such an understanding, to live in the way of God, walking in it and making oneself alive by it; for at once to be the way is to be life. Therefore the Savior says, 'I am the way and the life' (John 14:6).
And since the Son is the righteousness of the Father, he says this regarding one desiring to live in the Son; for the righteousness of God is revealed in him from faith to faith (Rom 1:17).

He says only that it is sufficient for us to be comforted in afflictions to have the promise of true life; 'fulfill this for us.' For if in this life only we are hoping in Christ, we are more to be pitied than all men, because we suffer evil now and not in expectation of a life to come. But the life that is to come is a resuscitation, since the soul itself is not life, nor is it true life.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Stability of Righteousness and Divine Life
english: We learn, if indeed the soul is not a human. For if it had the truth of living in its own life, the dead would not need resuscitation. Therefore the Lord said to the dead to live as if they did not yet have life, except insofar as they are in the power of the life-giving God; and he says they are lost if they do not happen to have a resurrection, saying he will raise his own, so that the one from it might not be lost. And Paul similarly says, 'If there is no resurrection of the dead, then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished' (1 Cor 15:17). For God did not give a life to the soul from the beginning as incorporeal, but immediately the one in the body, having breathed the breath of life into the body.

Regarding Psalm 118:53, to the sinner, godliness is a laughing matter, but to the God-fearing, lawlessness is a terror, because he foresees the dread of punishment. Regarding Psalm 118:54, he says, 'To me, also, the judgments looking toward your commandments are my only consolation, and your precepts, being taken up through song, bring cheer and lead to joy' (Ps 118:54). And I have known this alone as one who will dwell in a foreign and strange land and is truly unable to have any good, because for a stranger, houses are longed for, and before the return to these things, all is sorrowful.

Regarding Psalm 118:73, God does not twist the justice of man like a potter, even if it is said he twists; rather, whatever a potter works, he makes such by the power of the one working such a shape; and the present-day 'moldings' must be referred back to that first molding, such as 'Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you' (Jer 1:5); just as Job says, 'You formed me from clay' (Job 10:9), indicating the clay-molding in Adam regarding himself. Prayer regarding the making is thanksgiving, but following this is the power of the intellect which understands the commandments. Concerning this, Paul also says, 'Understand what I say: for the Lord will give you understanding in all things' (Rom 11:33). But treat the request as if toward a Creator: 'Care for your handiwork, and complete with intellect the living thing that is intellectual; and that which you prepared for indwelling with yourself, make it indwell through your knowledge of Your purposes.' Since from the beginning, man was in need of that which, of the many commands, made his mind unsuited to them, and indeed, having been made unstable, he needs those which fulfill the greater.

For without training in many evils and without the hope of God's helping, a man cannot stand firmly in virtue, for those competing are easily shaken when the struggle comes. Thus, he recognizes the strengthening from many sufferings, the strengthening of God's providence; then he asks for rest from his labors, saying, 'Let your mercy come that it may comfort me according to your word' (Ps 118:83).

Perhaps the righteous become more dead than living under afflictions, as if they resemble ascetics rather than men, losing their souls like dust being blown about, while choosing the hot and the practical way, as it is said elsewhere, 'I sat in darkness as if dead to the age' (Ps 118:84); but even while undergoing this, he says, I have not departed from God-taught righteousness, just as Joseph guarded righteous temperance. He calls the commandments 'promises.' He says, 'With courage, I seek the help from you, my God, through your promises and their truth' (Ps 118:86).

He asks for life, not yet eternal life, but the present life, worthy of not being handed over to the hands of the schemers unto death (Ps 118:88). He does not ask for this as an end, but as a means to a good end, for he says, 'I will guard the commands of God,' through which it is also possible to acquire eternal life. 'I will cling to your laws,' he says (Ps 118:93). For in them is life found, just as you have said to me, 'He who has made them, man, shall live in them.'

Thus the righteous lives alone even if he seems to have died, but the unrighteous are dead even if they seem to live. For the former have the constitution of life within them, which is righteousness, but those not having this resemble soulless things moved not by themselves but from without, because their life is from without, and they do not even have one life within them. Therefore the Lord himself, being truly righteousness, declares himself to be life, and says those not partaking of him do not have life within themselves; and the death of the Savior is not only life but is life-giving, becoming the release of men from death. The unrighteous, moreover, are blind to the beauty of righteousness and the majesty of the words concerning it.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exegesis of Psalm 118
english: And they do not see it as becoming; but he who, desiring these things and being of these, is established alone in understanding, that even to those lovers of her wisdom reveals her own beauty according to 'She loved me' (Ps 118:99), and 'will honor you; honor her, so that she may take hold of you' (Ps 118:100).

All things through study are beautiful in man, whence also the command regarding study was extended, as if through this one were to surpass the elder and the younger and the disciple [surpassing] the teachers. Presenting himself humble and obedient, he asks for the salvation upon this from God, on account of the one giving to the humble and having promised mercy to those who love him (Ps 118:107).

A greater proof than readiness is to go even through dangers without departing from the law, and being in attacks, not to be pulled away from the righteous [path] by anger and provocation toward the attackers, just as Saul's attack did not lead David astray from defending what was fitting (Ps 118:109-110).

He extended the demonstration of zeal concerning the law, since he said the law was set as a proper inheritance, not for a season but to live in all things approaching this, as not under any yoke of necessity but holily in the joy of the soul. For this indeed is both lasting and difficult to change, that which is done in joy.

Even if they are not hated according to man, it is not worthy of God to be called hated according to God such as these, according to 'You hated all workers of iniquity' (Ps 118:113), so that it is a greatest proof of loving the law to hate those who have strayed from the law; therefore also for Jehoshaphat, friendship toward such a one became a reproach through the prophet, because he loved the one hated by God (Ps 118:118-119). It shows an imitation of God. If even to God all the apostate of the decrees is exhausted by vain thoughts, and to Him they are accused as crown-wearers or dung-gatherers, being no more honorable; therefore also toward the love of the divine...
Disorders are raised up, the vanity of evils for the purpose of exhortation, taking care regarding the good. And the E edition was nothing reckoned.

By the non-evilness of God, the lacking is intended to be filled, waiting for Him, the good-working which is still to come, just as one guaranteeing this as it is to be fulfilled, just as those guaranteeing debts do so so as not to fall hard by deceits (Ps 118:122). 'Ally, raise up your servant to good' (Ps 118:129), and Akylas and Theodotion have guaranteed.
Others, he says, marvel at gold and precious stones, but I, standing only upon the wonderful and the good, have this and more importantly preserve all the divine commands as a treasure (Ps 118:130).

The words need opening; therefore also the Lord opened the mind of the disciples to understand the Scriptures, and the understanding given through the words keeps them away from the deception of pleasure or glory (Ps 118:130).
This also is requested, since even in disturbances and sorrows, the precision regarding the healthy word is difficult (Ps 118:134).
See the enmity which the righteous have (Ps 118:139). And this was against their injustice and the forgetting of the law.

It is possible, according to history, to refer the things contained here to David, saying these things about himself. For he was the shortest of all the sons of Jesse, but also being despised. For all his brothers having been taken by the father to where Samuel had prepared the table, David was among his father's sheep, not having been taken to the feast; but even though being younger and despised, he himself obtained the kingdom by the will of God, since the rights of God had not been neglected. And he was younger, and he who is being instructed in the divine words and being despised because of humbling himself, and the people called from among the Gentiles after the elder and the firstborn of Israel, should have shouted out the spoken word. For they despise him...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Joy of the Dwelling and the Unity of the Inhabitants
english: Guarding the rights of God by uncircumcised memory (Ps 118:162).

The word has its own meaning for David, that being pursued by Saul in vain and through envy, he ceased to resist through fear toward God; and it extends to the common experience, that of the wars of rulers there is no other way to be escaped from being harmed than by being guarded by the fear of God. After the gift of wisdom, he asks again for salvation from dangers (Ps 118:173); this too is a reward for the voluntary zeal concerning the divine law (Ps 118:174-175).

Thus, he was saying that he expected eternal salvation, and now he observes that this study of the law is being performed with longing. For he says that he will indeed seek and praise God through His all-wise judgments, having been helped by this, which is Christ, descending in place of men to death for the salvation of men, and being driven out to suffer, redeeming those in sufferings and those dying through death; following which, the 'My soul shall live' and the following verses follow (Ps 119:2).

This was indeed immediately after the first apostasy of man when Cain struck down his brother by deceit, but it is also through the whole age of the present, as is shown in other things and in this present matter. Therefore, the man who turns toward God, suffering and being afflicted, asks for salvation from Him. He does not foresee the scarcity lying then, when he shall be brought up to the dwelling of the city of peace and the citizenship with both the good and the bad (Ps 119:5).

Another also makes manifest the foreign land from one part, into which Israel, having fallen, dwelt, and indeed his sojourning to extend for the longest time. Prophesying in lamentation, he brings this forth as reaching even to the present established state; for this is the longest (Ps 119:7).

For the good and God-fearing ones make their own peace and with all men, when they do not lack the critical punishment which God had commanded against the Canaanites and Amorites, forbidding friendship toward them; but the wicked and those ignoring God would never come into friendship with the good, but they loathe godliness and do not favorably receive even the good things from the God-fearing, nor are they moved by the philanthropy of them (Ps 120:1b). Mountains, say...
There are the unsetting and heavenly powers there; and while waiting for help through these, he says that help does not spring from these, but from the Creator.

Regarding Ps 121:1b, joy is to hear what is said by the angels, namely those speaking to the prophets, such as the flocks beginning the Israelite [process], which is he who is shown through Zechariah, both acting as an ambassador on behalf of the fallen Jerusalem and speaking of its coming habitation. This is indeed what the singer says he heard and was made glad by, having foreseen the stable habitation in the holy city, perceiving it prophetically as the matter is present. For this is the 'Our feet have been standing in the courts of Jerusalem' (Ps 122:2). But the standing of feet is an immovable habitation, which even the holy prophets proclaim, whereas the opposite was when, according to history, God shook the foot of Jerusalem from its inhabited land. Therefore the singer speaks of the desolation of the city, having seen it just as Ezekiel did, but of the building up as a city being united, not according to the usual way, namely by surrounding it with walls, but by the inhabitants being united to one another. Therefore also he has not said 'a city', but as a city having a togetherness together. For neither does Ezekiel foretell that it shall be inhabited by walls, nor does Zechariah, but without walls; rather its wall shall be the Lord, because God is the guardian and companion of the unity of the saints. He interprets then the being through them of the inhabitants as the union, saying, 'There the tribes ascended, tribes of the Lord, a testimony to Israel to confess in the name of the Lord' (Ps 122:4). Not that they surrounded walls, and because of this they were united, but that they were united through themselves. A testimony indeed to Israel, namely testifying the truth of the promises, but to confess in the name of the Lord, meaning that to him who fulfilled the wonderful promise, a confession of graces is owed by those being benefited. He says that thrones of the house of David were established upon it, since even a kingdom is prophesied by Daniel, not only a principality of someone or the rule of one, but a common rule for the best and most God-fearing, through whom the kingdom of David is restored by the grace of Christ, who gave to the twelve apostles the right to judge, sitting upon the twelve thrones.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Commentary on Psalms
english: Israel. Regarding Psalm 124:3, evil people will not be allowed to destroy the good subjects, but after the good have suffered a little from them, He will free them from harmful slavery, which will not dare to fall upon those beginning under God. Regarding Psalm 126:1-2, Solomon is inscribed to the song because he built the temple. But he signifies the true Solomon, our Lord, the cause of the true and peaceful building. Therefore, this building is also shown to be god-made, and the firm guard in guarding according to God; and this is fitting, since the buildings, guards, and night-watches through men were passing into vainness, and the daytime care and toil. Therefore, such human things came forward so that the divine alone might be known to possess the firm and unchangeable, just as justice came through law so that God's justice might be shown with it, having the genuine and the only true, and true life after that which is in shadow and in image. When He gives sleep to His beloved, He has revealed the rest from God, resembling sleep, which will be given out of love.

Regarding Psalm 126:4a, 'Indeed, You have made me,' he says, 'Judah, as a bow to myself.' And here he speaks of the arrows of the Mighty toward the remaining saints against those lower than the ungodly and with injustice violent.

Regarding Psalm 127:1, many and various are the ways of entrance, and many-sided are the lives of those beginning, but one is the perfection reaching the summit. He characterizes those fearing the Lord, whoever they are, having said thus: 'Those walking in His ways.' For those not doing this do not fear the Lord. For the fear of the Lord is a turning away from evils, but he who is turned away from evils is ready for the divine ways.

Regarding Psalm 129:1b-2, it is possible for that from the depth, like waters, of the poured-out afflictions, but the endurance and the repetition of the same, being surpassed and being exhausted, and not willing to lift up the supplication because of desire. Therefore, 'Hear my voice and let your ears be attentive.' Regarding Psalm 131:6, to David, who had not foreseen, the place became manifest from the matter itself.

Therefore, 'We have heard and found,' he says, that God showed the threshing floor to Ornathan, upon which the altar was built to prevent the decaying death of the Hebrew race (Ps 131:8). Having loved the discovery as having known that which was desired of old, he rejoices in the thing and loves the worship there. It is there that he says God's presence occurs, because the glory of God became manifest through the presence of the angel.

Similarly, he says, he foretells the time concerning Solomon (Ps 131:9), in which the ark is moved from the tent and is established in the temple, and a divine glory shone and a cloud covered the house. These things, he says, we see to have happened to Solomon according to the words of David (Ps 131:10). For the favor is toward David (Ps 131:10). Even if the blessing is toward those after him, just as it is said in opposition to Solomon, that because of David all his kingship shall not fall, and indeed it has passed even to the descendants because of David's mercy, just as it is said concerning Hezekiah, 'I am a shield for this city because of David my servant' (2 Kings 22:20).

To the former and briefer gifts, it brings the greatest, being a preservation of all those (Ps 132:15). For he gave abundance of food from the beginning, which is called Thiran, though another interprets it as grain. And he promises to make the inhabitants satisfied, and he has made the counsel of priests and holy ones to be saved and to preside with the holy hymns. But of all these, having already been corrupted, and the nation being unable to enjoy even the good things of the earth because of the Roman authority, with the priesthood falling away and all the joy in the temple being dissolved, the great power—the horn of David, which has the power to gore all enemies, a fitting lamp shining with heavenly light for David and for his race, who, having begun at once upon all the world, sends out the torch, just as the prophet Simeon says, 'A light for revelation to the Gentiles and glory for your people Israel' (Luke 2:32).

And the parable was of a divine matter, and that of the ointment; but the one from God is more prominent, according to the parable of the dew falling from heaven upon the mountains. For the gift and the good thing are heavenly, not human, nor appearing among men apart from the gift from above.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Likeness of God and the Stewardship of the Land
english: The work of hymns signifies the gathering of all saints (Ps 133:1-2), neither by day nor by night, as sleep does not overcome them by the power of those then incorruptible and tireless bodies.

Hymns are the end of good things, while the works of God are the hypothesis of hymns, being gifts and benefits (Ps 134:1-2). Those who hymn are not strangers or those standing far off, but those present and remaining, just as David established the hymn-singers as those staying upon this.

If anyone says that the indwelling of humans by God is a great benefit and the capital of all benefits (Ps 134:3-4), just as He made the Hebrews His own people and a chosen people for Himself above all nations then, setting them apart as something more and surpassing, as also He is His own God in intimacy, the God of all in creation.

He recalls the things happening paradoxically concerning Israel (Ps 134:6-7)—not things that would appear by nature from the beginning, but by the will of the One above nature (this indeed of the heavens, such as fire, hail, and darkness; this of the earth, such as frogs, locusts, gnats, and the punishing energy against the firstborn; and this of those in the sea and the depths, such as those concerning the Red Sea)—to the creative power, linking these as having come from the same power, asserting that He alone is the one moving the clouds from the ends of the earth, kindling lightning, sending the precursors of rains, and sending winds from the invisible beginning; He says that the generation of winds is an unseen and unknown treasure of God, not known beforehand where they are before they blow; he continuously understands that the winds lie as in the bodies, having treasures.

The terrible things signify not only what happened for Israel's sake, but for the knowledge of God through all the earth and all time (Ps 134:13), not only while the works of the one doing them were being made known, but also later through memory.

Therefore, he names those above as gods according to the custom of the nations, though they are not gods; but now, to the shame of the false gods' idols, he names them by the matter, accusing that silver...

And it is like gold, purified by labor, because it is like that which is under men and the soulless, along with the vanity of souls, due to the absence of a life-giving spirit upon them; all such things possess the outward appearance of contempt, and the demons have the outward indictment that they are not gods, whose such likenesses exist. For the likeness of God is divine; therefore also man is the icon of the divine, not one sustained by divinity.

Not less than subduing the warring ones, to feed them in the wilderness and to lead them without supplies, and the cutting down of the Amorite kings, is a demonstration of the mercy of God, providing a place for habitation, giving to the Hebrews their land (Ps 135:16, 22). And this was the storing up of the wealth of the ungodly for the righteous. For they would not have been destroyed otherwise if they had not been coming to the fullness of sins, just as God said to Abraham; and Moses indeed says that he has not held Israel in possession of their land because of his own righteousness, but because of their lawlessness and through the love of God toward the fathers, so that toward them indeed the destructive judgment was to be just, but toward these a philanthropic beneficent giving, and for the participation in philanthropy, the piety of the fathers had become a preparation. For thus justly and goodly and fittingly into order things from God appear.

That they are lying in the wilderness shows just as the state of the captives is after the migration from their own cities (Ps 136:1, 2). For this is: 'At the willow trees we hung up our instruments' (Ps 136:2).

And according to the spiritual worship, they considered foreign lands to be the foreign souls, and to be kept in these, to bring forth the divine things, just as being migrated from one's own place into a foreign place, as the divine mouth of Christ says: 'Do not give the holy things to the dogs, nor cast your pearls before the swine' (Matt 7:6). Such was also Herod, desiring to behold the signs of Christ, not seeking this for reverence but for pleasant spectacle, wherefore he did not succeed.

'I will not use another land like yours, O Jerusalem,' he says, 'nor will I place on an equal the unclean with the pure, nor the profane near the holy; but for me, even being outside your habitation, your [one] will approach' (Ps 136:4, 5).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Destruction of Babylon and the Church of the Nations
english: Desire: and whenever I am transferred from this, my whole power is transferred. Because of this, those directing their prayers toward Jerusalem did everything possible in their prayers wherever they were brought, according to the requests of Solomon and the divine promises, just as it is necessary for us to turn toward the heavenly Jerusalem.

For it is not right for the instrument of words to fail (Ps 136:6), if it does not receive [them] toward what is necessary. Therefore, the blessed men also set their whole life upon the care of hymns (Ps 136:5), saying, 'I will sing to the Lord in my life, I will sing to my God as long as I exist.' And the city is precious to them because of the worship of God established in it, just as it is foretold: 'For the sake of the house of my God, I sought good things for you' (Ps 136:2).

For the highest and purest part of joy is placed in remembering the holy city. Thus, it will happen that the coming good joys will be, just as the Lord introduces to us the holy foods before the common and bodily [ones].

The righteous pray to be brought what the Babylonians have plundered (Ps 137:8). For this is the holy judgment: the sinner was caught in the works of His hands, making judgments by the [phrase] 'The Lord knows judgments' (1 Kings 18:40). Blessed indeed is he who is shown able to do this, through whom God manifests the righteous judgment, and He will turn against those who plundered to be plundered, and against those who raised up [violence] to be overthrown. For the service belongs to God, and blessed is the one serving God.

And it must be applied with knowledge and proper intention, so that Cyrus does not bless the Persian king who conquered Babylon, because he neither knew the grace by which he took strength over them, nor the one who gave it, God ('For you did not know me,' he says [Matt 7:23]), nor did he understand through the forgiveness of Israel into [the power]...

If being led away, as it is prophesied through Jesus; but the blessing will surround those who repay Babylon in kind, and those who fasten the infants of it to the rock and lift them up. For in truth, the first thing was blessed: not to ever behold Babylon nor to be in the confusion of its evils; but if once anyone became in it, having fallen from the better ones, he would be blessed if he would do what he has suffered and would counter-imprison the Babylonians and lead their very souls into the fear of God; and if even their infants he would not allow to grow but would crush them against the rock, he would become much more blessed.

But the infants of Babylon are the seeds of wickedness and the beginnings of the confused sins—not to be called sins—which indeed the saving Word (for the rock was Christ) seeks to annul by not allowing them to grow nor to proceed into works, he who is blessed in these things. Regarding Israel, a correction of the things concerning him lies ahead, as the prophecies say; but a second Church, coming out of all the nations, enters, leaving behind a land for those who will return from Jerusalem.

So also in the present matters, we heard fully of the captivity of the nation and a prayer for the punishment of those who captured them, but now the song follows, announcing the appearance of the word of God throughout all the inhabited world, just as in Isaiah the prophet, when the word was being taken away, Zion became a desert and a curse; immediately the knowledge of God is pre-announced among the other nations, according to 'I was made manifest to those not asking, I was found by those not seeking' (Isa 49:6). Such a disposition and such a composition of these songs existed, after the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Grace and the Unity of Soul and Body
english: For Israel, there is a prayer of thanksgiving, following hymns and foretold worships toward God, because through His mercy and His truth, for the sake of the name of the Word of God, He is being glorified—that is, what is now being fulfilled—to be glorified in the name of the Word as He was never previously glorified, since the worship of God was confined to a portion of the earth before the manifestation of the Word. The Creator is praised by all, and God was announced to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; He possessed this knowledge and honor even unto the nation of the Hebrews. But when His living Word came forth from God and was revealed into the world through a body, then every nation and the whole inhabited world rushes toward the worship of God, serving in the name of the Word and glorifying God in the presence of the Word; now reverence abounds among the nations according to the mercy, while it is also preserved for Israel according to the truth of the promises.

Psalm 137:3 shows great favor, and swift obedience in the name of Christ, and the provision of power being given to souls. For Christ says, 'If you ask anything in my name, I will do it' (John 14:14); and the apostle says that the provision of the Spirit comes to those who believe. Psalm 137:5 Let the providence of God be praised, because He is a great God, and His greatness is revealed through providence, just as through the seraphim His glory in the present providence and economy is praised, crying out, 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth' (Isaiah 6:3), ful—
For all the earth is his glory (Ps 137:6).

He says that human creation enjoys the gift of God, even this lesser and formerly more dishonored creature, which is not now itself exalted, because to God all things are lowly and the highest, and these are known from afar because the unapproachable height of God cannot be approached. Since all things are small in relation to God, it is nothing to wonder that even the smallest things are reached by his benefits; that is, those in the world who have no hope and are atheists, whom the apostle has spoken of as not even existing (Ps 137:7-8a).

Second, the part of Israel is brought forward, having been received into afflictions but to be repaired unto salvation; through which your enemies shall be struck by God, but they themselves shall attain the salvation from God. The Lord will repay on my behalf; for he will repay on behalf of the wronged of the nation so that they may come out from the hands of the oppressors (Ps 137:8c).
Even if we do not provide fruits worthy of your love, he says, because we are sinful works, we deserve not to be despised (Ps 137:8c).

Here, both soul and body are shown placed into one thing and molded under one [form], each setting the other, for he says that God has the knowledge of the psychic properties from the molding, just as another has said, 'He who formed the spirit of man in him' (Ps 138:5). For the creation is not in a state of separation, but even if the making of the soul is more beautiful than that of the body, it is not such as to be man-made according to the formation of matter, but is inspired according to the subsistence from divine power. Altogether, indeed, into one...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Prayer for Cleansing and the Judgment of the Wicked
english: He brings together more things, just as the name of a single thing sometimes participates in the common, and sometimes in the flesh being so named; just as the apostle, speaking of man as the image of God (Gen 1:26) because of the one having come into him from God which did not happen to a woman, clearly includes both soul and body, just as the male is distinguished from the female.

For example, also regarding Jonah, he fell into the sea while fleeing, and how he found the power of God regarding the movement of the waters, raising waves (Ps 138:9-10), and regarding the nature of living things, a sea-monster receiving him and not crushing him, and him being guarded in the sea-monster and undergoing no destruction.

'You know my substance,' he says, 'and the joining of my bones is your work (Ps 138:15-16); in the secret of a mother's womb, as if a land being variegated within, you knew me before I was formed; and I have been written by you as in a book, and every complete human being is being created by measured time in a quantity of days (Ps 138:17-18)'; which is indeed a wonder of order and of precise symmetry, that life-giving is being given without lacking a single day.

And I was not said to be short, they say, because the righteous are found to be few according to each season, but toward the whole multitude they were seen to be many who existed from eternity, and I saw them in great number and more in count, whom the resurrection will show as countless, and especially now having increased in multitude at the presence of Christ, according to the filling of the whole earth with knowledge (Hab 2:14).

the Lord, and I will praise You in a great assembly; among a heavy people, I will magnify You (Ps 138:23-24). Since there are things precious to You among the righteous men and laid up for eternal glory, but for the destruction of the wicked, I beseech You to be cleansed of all evil by the cleansing from You, since You are able to powerfully cleanse us even in the evils into which we fall through our ignorance.

Therefore, he says, lead me through good deeds upon which eternal life shall be stored up, cleansing me from every evil that leads toward destruction (Ps 139:9). It is fitting for God that it should be said that no mindset be granted to lawlessness, nor should they be permitted against righteousness, nor should the bitter and destructive [things] reach an end for them and be forgiven, but rather these things should be held fast upon which they possess bitterness. For when injustice occurs, it is much more difficult and it will increase the blasphemy against the righteousness of God (Ps 139:11).

And they will fall into a fall, not like the fall of the righteous who fall and rise again, but an unrelenting [fall] that no longer comes toward a resurrection; they will be brought into nothingness, unable to become established upon the earth, but being thrust out from it in corrupting punishments (Ps 140:2).

If in the morning we understand the life that is passing by in rest and glory, let us consider the one that is present in night and evening (Ps 140:2); in the evening, as if having some light remaining, for the sake of the knowledge of the good and the gifts from God, but at night, according to the darkness of evil and the tyranny of the rulers of this darkness. Therefore, man now needs an intense cry, because he has been struck.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Separation of the Spiritual
english: He is weighed down by darkness and by the evils that are present, toward the only One able to enlighten, and to show the dawn from the evening and the day from the night, and to effect a transformation of the evil works (Ps 140:4-5). Therefore, He makes a statement concerning evil, desiring to be pure from it and to be a stranger to those living in this [life]. For the wounds of friends are more trustworthy than the voluntary kindnesses of enemies (Ps 140:6-7). For, he says, they mock the beautiful and that very thing which is most beautiful by confession, diverting prayer according to their own will. And this, he says, will leave them uprooted from the earth, just as [a plant] having been thrust out through a rock and having its root displaced. And they set a laugh and a joy upon my words, laughing at the solemn things because of rejoicing with the immodest, and through long-standing habituation to these things, the petition is cut off concerning the beautiful and truly desirable and pleasant things. Secondly, regarding death, he speaks, recounting the sorrowful dissolution of man, saying that as a fragment is scattered when broken (Ps 140:10).

The Deliverer: Let the lawless fall into their own nets. Into them, he says, let the devices be frequent, but not upon us who are innocent. And I, he says, shall turn away from the mingling with the wicked, until I am able to escape them as well. For this is safety: to not be defiled by them at all, to not even approach, nor even to mingle with them. This also Jeremiah says of a good man when he bears a yoke in his youth: he will sit alone and be silent. But now for us, the separation from the wicked is spiritual, since the bodily [separation] is impossible; for we ought, then, to come out from the world, as Paul says (Ps 141:2).

Truly, the unity of the Dyad is also good, having placed the Lord and God upon such a thing; yet more knowable to those who have learned the perfection is the apprehension of the Dyad in unity, which Paul presents, explaining one God and one Lord, who, being two, are perceived to unite the God in [the] Lord and the Lord in God; according to which the divine and sovereign essence is observed in identity, moving from Father into Son according to the divine, and from Son into God being led up according to the sovereign. (Ps 141:8). Not by fleeing the siege by enemies is the end set, but to offer up something even more beautiful for the sake of God; for this indeed is the most supreme end (Ps 142).

Others say that the psalm is not unattributed, but is inscribed 'A Psalm of David, when the son persecuted him.' However, this does not apply to all the interpretations. But the things being said are not foreign; nor does it prevent one from speaking concerning the persecution by Saul (Ps 142:8ab). But according to the whole hypothesis of the life of the righteous, or the perfect mercy, it is not yet received, but rather the coming appearance that promises in the morning, when the Master will shine upon the righteous appearing from heaven (Ps 142:11). The name of the goodness of the salvation of God becomes a pretext for Himself, according to the apostle saying, 'To the praise of the glory of His grace' (Ps 142:11).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Power and Human Limitation
english: But all things are similar: human things are one kind, while the examples of divine energy—terrible and strong and destructive to men—are another (Ps 143:4-5).

In this present life, according to the succession of one man, these things can be so, because those succeeding enter into the place of those departing; therefore we are all called by the name of Adam as if we were that same person, and God says, 'I made earth and man upon it,' counting all as one (Ps 144:1). But according to the life to come, these things are true for each one, with God being perpetually and eternally praised; and since it is not sufficient to praise for a little while, He adds 'unto the age and unto the age of ages.'

Since all that God has made remains for ever according to the Preacher (Eccl 3:14), every generation seeing His works praises them, seeing them to be surpassing all praise (Ps 144:4). And they declare Your power, by which You brought them into existence. This is the wisdom by which You have made all things; and Your power and wisdom is Your only-begotten offspring; for Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.

They know that He has dominion over all, even if He does not yet manifest this to men who possess it receptively (Ps 144:9, 12). For men are small regarding the manifestation of the majesty of the divine kingdom within them; therefore, what is becoming for God is brought forth (Ps 144:12).

Saying 'the hands of God' (Ps 144:16), He means the opening of the provision of the food of created things; it is clear He is not presenting physical hands, but the creative [power] thus imitating. For if not through all things, He says, the Philanthropy is perceived (Ps 144:17), but many things that are pleasant and salvific, as well as many that are laborious and corruptible, come to those—such as the distinction of fruits, the destructive generations of beasts, and diseases.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Justice and the Nature of True Life
english: These are the down-payments; yet none of these are outside of justice, well interwoven with goodness, so as not to let the zeal for the beautiful perish through a lawless, unchecked cheerfulness (Ps 144:21). Again, he stretches out the hymns over a long duration and does not stand upon a single point or his own person, but intends to make all men equal toward the infinite age, even if he is sometimes seen along with those who are passing away, signifying a fellowship of the righteous who have become God's beginning according to the apostle (Ps 145:1-2).

It seems to teach that this is the work of life, and this is the benefit of being, if we are joined to the truly living and to the truly existing Being; for this is the provision both for the truly living and for existing eternally, since from the present life we are brought toward the life that is to come (Ps 145:5). In this way, hope in men is vanity, but hope in God is blessedness. For He is a true helper, eternal and ruler of all things; in this, His authority is such that, as from abundant wealth and infinite greatness, He readily benefits (Ps 146:4).

He is so great and so far-reaching that even the unnumbered stars are not outside His knowledge, but having been regulated by Him, He precisely knows the nature and power of each, distinguishing them just as names of designations (Ps 146:5). Strength and understanding, indeed, we hear in human terms, but let us not think in human terms what strength is, by which a strong man acts, nor what understanding is, by which the wise man deliberates, being something both arriving and departing.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fullness of Wisdom and Power
english: He possesses what is powerful and wise. For as God, He is not so powerful and wise as one who has nothing more beautiful or less within himself, such as power and wisdom filled with power and full of wisdom, being entirely the most perfect; and for this reason, He does not have power and wisdom filling him, but rather possesses a fullness proceeding from himself.

Just as Solomon calls wisdom offspring and presents self-wisdom having come to him from God, he teaches that because the creatures came to be through wisdom, the generator of wisdom is something greater than the creation of itself. To this, the long-standing excellence of the relation to the works, having ascended far above that which accompanies the creator, was fitting, since it is impossible to conceive of anything greater than the greatest; so that what is perceived as the greatest is that all things have come forth from the relation to the works, and this concerns the Father of wisdom and power.

And so great is His strength and understanding, as being from Him and with Him as offspring, fruit, and son, not as having happened in Him, concerning which it has been said, 'Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God' (1 Cor 1:24). And since wisdom is the power itself, having a synonymy with understanding, in which He made the heaven according to what was said—He who made the heaven in understanding—so that His strength and understanding are great, the understanding of God is unsearchable and countless, whence it is written, 'O depth of riches and wisdom' (Rom 11:33).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Incomprehensibility of God and the Praise of Creation
english: of the knowledge of God. For His understanding is so deep that, due to incomprehensibility, it has no number. And even if it is said to have no number because of the exceeding multitude of things contemplated within it, you yourself will realize this (Ps 148:2).

The angels are indeed those in the heavens, but the powers are even above these, being fitting for the Highest, existing to proclaim [His glory] to men; and they alone possess continuous blessedness through the stability which is from God, which are also those called thrones by the apostle, being established by God's name and being subject to the Divine and being great in creation; having always stood firm and being a spring in the reception of the Divine glory.

Shine in the heaven with the day and the night, lighting it (Ps 148:3), that is, the highest heaven, which is the firmament according to Moses, and indeed the water above it; he is exhorted to praise God. It is clear that all these things are a hymn to God, manifesting the all-praised One of the Creator through their own beauty, power, and energy.
And saying to all the righteous, he shows those from every nation (Ps 148:14). By prophecy, as he drew Israel, because he had drawn near from the beginning, he shows the [inclusion of] the Gentiles.
Therefore, the rest after death and the rejoicing in this, the Word necessarily established (Ps 149:5), according to [the saying] 'In peace I will lie down and sleep' (Ps 4:8).
